scenario: YouTube 式视频平台的 Up Next 推荐：用户正在看一个视频时，系统要在旁边实时展示接下来推荐播放的视频列表。
q: 为什么当前正在观看的视频要作为 Up Next 排序的核心特征，而不能只依赖用户的长期兴趣画像？
options: 长期画像存储成本太高，系统负担不起
当前视频最直接反映此刻的意图，长期画像跟不上会话内的兴趣切换
当前视频的画质参数决定了排序结果
长期画像只对新用户有效，老用户必须完全换成当前视频特征
why: Up Next 是强上下文场景：用户刚表现出的兴趣比几周前积累的长期画像更能预测下一步。两者应结合，当前视频权重更高。
why_en: The video someone is watching right now signals their immediate intent far more directly than a slow-moving long-term profile.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Current[Current video] --> Rank[Up Next ranker]
  Session[Session history] --> Rank
  Profile[Long-term profile] --> Rank
options_en: Long-term profiles are too expensive to store, so the system can't afford them
The current video most directly reflects intent right now; a long-term profile can't keep up with in-session shifts
The current video's encoding quality determines the ranking
Long-term profiles only work for new users; returning users must switch entirely to current-video features
q_en: Why should the video someone is currently watching be a core feature for Up Next ranking, instead of relying only on their long-term interest profile?
scenario_en: On a YouTube-style video platform's Up Next panel, the system must show a live list of next-video recommendations while the user is watching.
optionExplanations: 存储成本不是决定因素——就算全存得起，长期画像更新慢仍跟不上当下兴趣切换。
当前视频是这一刻意图最直接的信号，比几周前攒的长期画像更新更快。
画质参数是编码属性，不是意图信号，把它当排序依据是把问题跑偏了。
当前视频特征对新老用户都同样重要，不是只有新用户才需要它。
optionExplanations_en: Storage cost isn't the real constraint — even if profiles were cheap to store, they'd still update too slowly to catch in-session shifts.
The current video is the most direct signal of intent right now, updating far faster than a long-term profile ever could.
Encoding quality is a technical video attribute, not an intent signal, so using it for ranking misses the point.
Current-video features matter for both new and returning users, not just newcomers.

scenario: 面试官给出约束：视频库约 1B 条、日活约 1B 用户、每次只展示约 5 个推荐位、从用户打开视频到展示 Up Next 列表只有约 250ms。
q: 这组规模和延迟约束最直接排除了哪种架构？
options: 先用候选生成把 1B 条缩小到几万，再逐级排序到 5 个
对每次请求都用一个重排序模型给全部 1B 条视频打分，再取分最高的 5 个
把候选生成结果和视频 embedding 提前离线算好、在线只做少量计算
用便宜的树模型先把候选量级从万级压到百级
why: 哪怕每条视频只花 1 微秒打分，1B 条也要 1 秒，远超 250ms 预算；必须先分阶段缩小候选，而不是对全库跑重模型。
why_en: Even at one microsecond per video, scoring one billion videos would take about a second, far more than the 250-millisecond budget, so a single full-catalog pass is impossible.
options_en: Shrink one billion candidates down to a few tens of thousands first, then rank down to five in stages
Score all one billion videos with a single heavy ranker on every request, then keep the top five
Precompute candidate-generation results and video embeddings offline, and do little compute online
Use a cheap tree model to shrink candidates from ten-thousands down to hundreds first

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

q_en: Given this scale and latency budget, which architecture does it rule out most directly?
scenario_en: The interviewer sets the constraints: about 1B videos, about 1B daily active users, roughly 5 recommendation slots shown at once, and only about 250ms from opening a video to showing the Up Next list.
optionExplanations: 候选生成本来就该做粗筛，把 1B 降到几万，这类分阶段设计正是延迟预算允许的做法。
对全部候选逐条跑重模型，光是打分耗时就冲到秒级，跟展示预算完全不在一个量级，是最先被约束卡死的架构。
预计算和缓存把大部分开销挪到线上请求之前，不占用 250ms 的在线预算，是被允许的。
树模型便宜到能在毫秒级筛掉大部分候选，不违反延迟约束，也是可行的一环。
optionExplanations_en: Shrinking candidates from 1B down to tens of thousands is exactly what staged funnels are for, and it fits the latency budget.
Scoring every candidate with the heavy model alone pushes total scoring time into the seconds range, nowhere near the serving budget, so it's the first architecture the constraint rules out.
Precomputing and caching moves most of the cost off the online request path, so it doesn't eat into the 250ms budget.
Cheap tree models can filter most candidates in milliseconds without breaking the latency constraint.

scenario: 你要为 Up Next 推荐定义业务目标；如果单纯优化点击率，标题党和夸张缩略图会被算法鼓励。
q: 作为业务目标，应该优化下面哪一个？
options: 最大化点击率，不管点击后的行为
只最大化广告曝光，不顾用户体验
最大化质量调整后的观看时长
只最大化平均视频时长本身
whenOtherWins: 如果产品是导航型搜索（用户想尽快找到答案并离开），快速完成任务可能比拉长观看时长更重要。
why: 质量调整后的 watch time 能兼顾平台收入和用户满意，避免只追点击或鼓励低质量的沉迷内容。
why_en: Quality-adjusted watch time balances platform revenue and user satisfaction better than raw click-through rate.
tradeoff: 点击率的可测量性 vs 质量调整后 watch time 的长期一致性
options_en: Maximize click-through rate, regardless of what happens after the click
Maximize ad impressions only, regardless of user experience
Maximize quality-adjusted watch time
Maximize average video length by itself
q_en: As the business objective, which of these should you optimize for?
scenario_en: You are defining the business objective for Up Next; if you optimize purely for click-through rate, clickbait titles and exaggerated thumbnails get rewarded by the algorithm.
optionExplanations: 只看点击率会把标题党、夸张缩略图训练成赢家，掩盖点击后满意度差的问题。
只顾广告曝光会牺牲用户体验，长期只会赶走用户、反噬广告库存本身。
质量调整后的观看时长把满意度和参与度都算进去，能同时兼顾平台收入和用户长期体验。
只看平均时长会鼓励硬拉长视频、甚至靠冗余内容凑时长，不代表真实满意度。
optionExplanations_en: Optimizing raw CTR alone trains the system to reward clickbait and exaggerated thumbnails, even when post-click satisfaction is bad.
Maximizing ad exposure alone sacrifices user experience, which eventually drives users away and hurts ad inventory itself.
Quality-adjusted watch time folds in satisfaction alongside engagement, balancing platform revenue with users' long-term experience.
Optimizing raw average video length just rewards padding videos out longer, without reflecting real satisfaction.

q: 为什么 CTR（点击率）不适合作为唯一的业务目标？
options: CTR 的埋点实现成本太高，难以稳定采集
CTR 会鼓励点击诱饵，点击后满意度差也照样得分
CTR 在数学上永远等于用户留存率
CTR 只能用于视频分类任务，不能用于排序
why: 用户可能被夸张缩略图吸引点击，但点击后很快离开。推荐系统要看点击后的满意度和长期效果，而不只是有没有点。
why_en: CTR alone can reward clickbait because it ignores what happens after the click, such as the user leaving immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，展示中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR is the click-through rate, the fraction of impressions that get clicked.

options_en: CTR is too expensive to instrument reliably
CTR rewards clickbait because it still scores well even when post-click satisfaction is poor
CTR is mathematically always equal to retention
CTR can only be used for video classification, not ranking
q_en: Why is CTR (click-through rate) a poor choice as the sole business objective?
optionExplanations: 埋点成本不是问题所在，CTR 真正的缺陷是它完全不管点击后用户满不满意。
CTR 只看有没有点，夸张缩略图能骗来点击，但用户点完可能秒退。
CTR 和留存率是两个独立指标，数学上不存在必然相等的关系。
CTR 是一个通用的参与度信号，同样能用在排序而不只是分类任务。
optionExplanations_en: Instrumentation cost isn't the issue — CTR's real flaw is that it ignores whether users were satisfied after clicking.
CTR only counts whether someone clicked; a misleading thumbnail can win the click even if the user bounces right after.
CTR and retention are separate metrics with no mathematical guarantee of ever being equal.
CTR is a general engagement signal that ranking can use too, not something limited to classification.
scenario: 你为 YouTube 首页排序做实验，CTR 涨了 8%，但次日回访率反而跌了 3%。
scenario_en: You're ranking the YouTube home feed: an experiment lifts CTR by 8 percent, but next-day return rate drops 3 percent.

q: 如果把观看时长（watch time）本身当成唯一优化目标，最大的风险是什么？
options: 系统会完全无法记录观看时长
可能推成瘾、低质量或偏长的视频，损害长期满意度和创作者生态
watch time 只对短视频平台有意义
watch time 会让系统必然更公平地分配曝光
why: 观看时长是不错的 proxy，但不是全部：纯优化它会偏向成瘾内容或更长视频，需要质量、满意度和多样性作为约束。
why_en: Raw watch time can promote addictive or unnecessarily long videos even when long-term user satisfaction actually suffers.
options_en: The system would be completely unable to record watch time
It can push addictive, low-quality, or overly long videos, hurting long-term satisfaction and the creator ecosystem
Watch time is only meaningful for short-video platforms
Watch time necessarily makes exposure more fairly distributed
q_en: If raw watch time itself is treated as the sole optimization target, what is the biggest risk?
optionExplanations: 系统完全能记录观看时长，问题不在能不能测，而在只优化它会带偏内容。
纯拉长观看时长会把成瘾但低质、或单纯注水变长的视频顶上去，伤害长期满意度和创作者生态。
watch time 对长短视频平台都适用，不是短视频独有的概念。
只优化时长不会让曝光更公平，反而可能让占用时间多的内容垄断推荐位。
optionExplanations_en: Watch time is easy to record — the risk isn't measurement, it's that optimizing it alone skews what gets recommended.
Pure watch-time optimization can push addictive-but-low-quality or artificially padded videos to the top, hurting long-term satisfaction and the creator ecosystem.
Watch time is a meaningful signal on both long- and short-form platforms, not just short video.
Optimizing for length alone doesn't make exposure fairer — it can let time-hogging content dominate recommendation slots.
scenario: 短视频平台把排序目标改成纯观看时长，两周后用户抱怨停不下来，优质短片曝光下降。
scenario_en: A short-video platform switches ranking to pure watch time; two weeks in, users say they cannot stop, and good short clips lose reach.

q: 一个更完整的视频推荐业务目标通常要同时平衡哪几方利益？（多选）
options: 用户满意度
创作者的可持续成长
平台的广告收入与整体健康
只服务当前最热门的那批内容
why: 推荐系统同时影响用户、创作者和平台三方，过度优化任何一方都可能长期损害其余两方。
why_en: Recommendation objectives usually balance user satisfaction, creator sustainability, and platform health together.
options_en: User satisfaction
Sustainable creator growth
Platform ad revenue and overall health
Serving only the current most popular content
q_en: A more complete video-recommendation business objective usually has to balance which parties' interests at the same time? (select all)
optionExplanations: 用户满意度差，推荐再精准也留不住人，是最基本的一方利益。
只讨好用户、不给创作者成长空间，供给端会枯竭、内容生态跟着萎缩。
平台收入和系统健康决定这套推荐能不能长期运营下去，不是纯慈善指标。
只服务当前最热门内容会让长尾创作者失去曝光机会，牺牲另外两方利益。
optionExplanations_en: If users aren't satisfied, no amount of ranking precision keeps them around — it's the most basic stakeholder.
Serving only users while starving creators of growth eventually dries up the content supply itself.
Ad revenue and platform health determine whether the whole system can keep running long-term, not just a nice-to-have.
Only serving currently-hot content starves long-tail creators of exposure, sacrificing the other two stakeholders.
scenario: UGC 视频平台的创作者流失率在上升，广告主也在抱怨内容质量，你要重定排序目标。
scenario_en: On a UGC video platform creator churn is rising and advertisers complain about content quality, so you're redefining the ranking objective.

q: 给定用户、当前正在看的视频和会话上下文，Up Next 推荐的 primary ML objective 应该是什么？
options: 判定当前账号是否为自动机器人账号
给候选排序，预测其长期满意度和参与度贡献
为视频内容自动生成字幕文本
压缩视频缩略图的文件体积大小
why: 系统要预测点击、观看、分享、回访等未来行为，再用 value model 把这些预测汇总成排序价值。
why_en: The primary ML objective is ranking candidate videos by predicted contribution to long-term engagement given the user, current video, and session.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Gen[10k candidates] --> Light[Light ranker]
  Light --> Keep[Keep top hundreds]
  Light --> Drop[Drop obvious misses]
  Keep --> Heavy[Heavy ranker]
options_en: Determine whether the current account is an automated bot account
Rank candidates by predicting their contribution to long-term satisfaction and engagement
Automatically generate caption text for video content
Compress the file size of video thumbnails
q_en: Given a user, the video they are currently watching, and session context, what should the primary ML objective for Up Next be?
optionExplanations: 判断账号是否为机器人是风控任务，和 Up Next 的排序目标完全不是一回事。
排序模型要预测候选视频对长期满意度和参与度的贡献，再据此给候选打分排序。
自动生成字幕是内容处理任务，不属于排序模型要解决的问题。
压缩缩略图文件体积是存储/传输优化，跟排序目标没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Detecting whether an account is a bot is a trust-and-safety task, unrelated to Up Next's ranking objective.
The ranker needs to predict each candidate's contribution to long-term satisfaction and engagement, then score and order candidates on that.
Auto-generating captions is a content-processing task, not something the ranking objective is solving.
Shrinking thumbnail file size is a storage/delivery optimization, unrelated to the ranking objective.
scenario: 用户正在看视频，播放结束前要给出 Up Next 列表，团队的北极星是长期留存而非单次点击。
scenario_en: A user is mid-video and you must produce the Up Next list before it ends; the team north star is long-term retention, not one click.

q: value model 在这套多阶段视频推荐系统里承担什么角色？
options: 完全替代候选生成层，直接从原始视频库里挑视频
把多个预测头组合成一个业务排序分
只负责统计数据库查询延迟
只在训练缩略图分类模型时使用
why: 重 ranker 会同时预测多种结果，value model 决定如何按业务目标把这些预测加权汇总成最终排序分。
why_en: A value model combines multiple predicted outcomes into one business-aligned ranking score used for the final ordering.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Cand[Hundreds of candidates] --> Features[Full features]
  Features --> Interact[Cross interactions]
  Interact --> Heads[CTR watch satisfaction]
  Heads --> Score[Final score]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个预测头输出按业务权重汇总成一个排序分数的模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A value model combines several predicted signals into one business-weighted ranking score.

options_en: Fully replace the candidate-generation layer and pick videos straight from the raw catalog
Combine several prediction heads into one business ranking score
Only track database query latency
Only get used for training a thumbnail classifier
q_en: What role does the value model play in this multi-stage video recommendation system?
optionExplanations: value model 不做候选筛选，它工作在重 ranker 已经打完分之后。
多个预测头各自输出一个信号，value model 是把这些信号按业务权重汇总成最终排序分数的那一层。
统计数据库查询延迟是运维监控的事，不是 value model 的职责。
value model 用在线上排序阶段，不是训练缩略图分类器的工具。
optionExplanations_en: The value model doesn't do candidate filtering — it works after the heavy ranker has already scored things.
Several prediction heads each output one signal, and the value model is the layer that combines them into a single business-weighted ranking score.
Tracking database query latency is an ops-monitoring concern, not something the value model does.
The value model operates in online ranking, not as a tool for training a thumbnail classifier.
scenario: 重 ranker 输出点击、观看时长、分享三个预测头，最终却只能给候选排出一个顺序。
scenario_en: The heavy ranker emits three heads — click, watch time, share — but the slate needs one single ordering.

q: 大规模视频推荐系统几乎都采用多阶段（候选生成→轻排→精排→重排）架构，而不是单一模型端到端处理，主要原因是什么？
options: 无法对十亿候选全部跑重模型，须逐级缩小候选集
多阶段架构训练起来天然更简单
单阶段架构在数学上无法训练收敛
多阶段架构纯粹是为了让架构图更完整
why: 候选生成先圈定可能相关的视频，轻 ranker 保召回降规模，重 ranker 追求质量，reranker 再调整整体 slate。
why_en: Large-scale recommendation uses multiple stages because scoring billions of items with the heaviest model is computationally infeasible within the latency budget.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Billion[1B videos] --> Gen[Generators]
  Gen --> Light[Light ranker]
  Light --> Heavy[Heavy ranker]
  Heavy --> Slate[Reranker slate]
options_en: It is infeasible to run a heavy ranker over billions of candidates, so the set must shrink in stages
A multi-stage architecture is naturally simpler to train
A single-stage architecture cannot mathematically converge during training
A multi-stage architecture exists purely to make the diagram look complete
q_en: Large-scale video recommenders almost always use a multi-stage architecture (candidate generation → light ranking → heavy ranking → reranking) instead of one end-to-end model. Why?
optionExplanations: 十亿候选全跑重模型算力扛不住，必须先用便宜阶段缩小候选集再上贵模型。
多阶段架构其实要训练和维护好几个模型，整体训练复杂度更高，不是更简单。
单阶段架构在数学上完全能收敛，问题出在算力和延迟，不是可训练性。
分阶段是延迟和成本约束逼出来的工程选择，不是为了让架构图好看。
optionExplanations_en: Running a heavy model over a billion candidates just isn't affordable, so cheaper stages have to funnel the pool down first.
Multi-stage systems actually mean training and maintaining several models, which is more complex overall, not simpler.
Single-stage architectures can converge mathematically just fine — the real blocker is compute and latency, not trainability.
Staging is an engineering response to latency and cost constraints, not something done to make the architecture diagram look complete.
scenario: 视频库有 10 亿条，重 ranker 单条打分约 1ms，而端到端延迟预算只有 250ms。
scenario_en: The catalog holds a billion videos, the heavy ranker costs about a millisecond per item, and the end-to-end budget is 250 milliseconds.

scenario: 视频库有上亿条，但重排序阶段在线只能接收几万个候选。
q: 候选生成层应该如何设计？
options: 只依赖全站热门榜单，不做任何个性化召回
用一个重排序模型直接对全库视频逐条打分
多路并行 generator：订阅、热门、个性化召回都覆盖
每次请求随机抽样少量视频充当候选，跳过召回逻辑
whenOtherWins: 如果产品只需要全站趋势榜（不追求个性化），单一热门 generator 可能就足够。
why: 多个 generator 各自覆盖不同的召回假设，能避免单一路径漏掉高质量候选；有限上下文的 generator 还可以预计算缓存。
why_en: Candidate generation should combine multiple parallel sources so that no single path misses a whole class of good candidates.
tradeoff: 召回覆盖面 vs 在线计算和维护成本
diagram:
flowchart TD
  G[Candidate generators] --> Sub[Subscriptions]
  G --> Similar[Similar videos]
  G --> Popular[Trending]
  G --> Vector[Personalized ANN]
  G --> Fresh[Fresh content]
options_en: Rely only on a single platform-wide trending list, with no personalized retrieval
Use one heavy reranking model to score every video in the catalog one by one
Run multiple parallel generators covering subscriptions, trending, and personalized retrieval
Randomly sample a handful of videos as candidates on every request, skipping retrieval logic
q_en: How should the candidate-generation layer be designed?
scenario_en: The video catalog has on the order of a billion items, but the reranking stage can only accept on the order of tens of thousands of candidates online.
optionExplanations: 只靠全站热门榜会让所有用户看到同样的东西，完全放弃个性化召回。
用重排序模型对全库逐条打分早就超出候选生成阶段能承受的延迟和算力。
订阅、热门、个性化各开一路 generator，任何一路看走眼时其他路径还能兜住，比单一来源更抗漏召回。
随机抽样候选完全跳过了召回逻辑，等于放弃了个性化和相关性。
optionExplanations_en: Relying only on a global trending list shows every user the same thing, abandoning personalization entirely.
Scoring the entire library with a reranking model already blows past the latency and compute this stage can afford.
Running separate generators for subscriptions, trending, and personalization means one path missing something doesn't sink the whole pool — more resilient than a single source.
Randomly sampling candidates skips recall logic altogether, giving up personalization and relevance.

q: 哪一类 candidate generator 更容易被预计算和缓存？
options: 依赖用户当前完整会话上下文、每次都要重新计算的实时个性化 generator
上下文有限或相对通用的 generator，例如全站热门榜、订阅作者的最新视频
每次请求都需要调用重排序模型的 generator
只能由人工每天挑选的候选列表
why: 上下文少或变化慢的结果可以提前算好存起来，降低在线延迟；高度个性化、实时的 generator 缓存难度更高。
why_en: Candidate generators with limited or slow-changing context are the ones that are easiest to precompute and cache.
options_en: A real-time personalized generator that depends on the user's full current session and recomputes every time
Generators with limited or fairly generic context, like the platform trending list or an author's newest uploads
A generator that must call the heavy ranker on every request
A candidate list that can only be curated by humans every day
q_en: Which kind of candidate generator is easiest to precompute and cache?
optionExplanations: 依赖完整会话上下文的实时 generator 每次输入都在变，没法提前缓存。
上下文少或变化慢的 generator（全站热门、订阅最新视频）结果可以提前算好存起来。
每次都调重排序模型的说法本身不成立，那是精排阶段的活，不是候选生成层。
人工挑选候选无法规模化，也不是候选生成的正常形态。
optionExplanations_en: A realtime generator tied to the full session context changes on every request, so there's nothing stable to precompute.
Generators with limited or slow-changing context — sitewide trending, an author's newest uploads — can be computed ahead of time and cached.
Calling the reranking model on every request describes the heavy-ranking stage, not what candidate generators do.
Manually curated candidates can't scale and aren't how candidate generation normally works.
scenario: 召回层 QPS 很高，你想把一部分 candidate generator 挪到离线预计算来省在线延迟。
scenario_en: Retrieval QPS is high, so you want to move some candidate generators offline into precomputed lists to save online latency.

scenario: 在做特征设计时你发现某个信号（比如“视频与用户历史兴趣的语义相似度”）能有效预测视频是否会被喜欢，但目前的候选生成层并没有覆盖这一类视频。
q: 这对候选生成层的设计提出了什么要求？
options: 既然是有效信号，重 ranker 自己就能把这类视频找出来
必须新增一个按该信号召回视频的 generator
这类信号只在训练阶段有用，和候选生成层无关
候选生成层的设计和特征质量没有关系
whenOtherWins: 如果候选池已经全量覆盖一个很小的目录，就不需要为每个信号单独建一个 generator。
why: ranker 只能给已经被召回的候选打分，如果没有 generator 覆盖某个信号对应的视频，这个信号再有效也发挥不了作用。
why_en: If a signal predicts relevance, a candidate generator must retrieve videos from that signal's region, because rankers can only score items that were already retrieved.
tradeoff: 为每个高价值信号新增 generator 的召回收益 vs 候选生成层的复杂度和维护成本
options_en: Since it's a valid signal, the heavy ranker alone can surface these videos on its own
A new generator must be added that retrieves videos using this signal
This kind of signal is only useful during training and has nothing to do with candidate generation
Candidate-generation design has nothing to do with feature quality
q_en: What does this imply about how the candidate-generation layer should be designed?
scenario_en: While designing features you find a signal — semantic similarity between a video and the user's historical interests — that predicts whether a video will be liked, but the current candidate-generation layer doesn't retrieve videos along that dimension at all.
optionExplanations: 重 ranker 只能给候选池里已有的视频打分，池子外面的视频它连看都看不到。
召回阶段没圈到的视频压根进不了候选池，排序模型再强也无从谈起给它打分。
训练阶段和线上召回用的是同一批信号，不存在只在训练有用的说法。
候选生成层的召回假设直接决定哪些信号能被利用，两者密切相关。
optionExplanations_en: The heavy ranker can only score videos that are already inside the candidate pool — anything outside it, the ranker never even sees.
A video the recall stage never pulls in can't reach the candidate pool at all, so no matter how strong the ranker is, it never gets a chance to score it.
The same signal used at training time is the one used online, so there's no such thing as a training-only signal.
The candidate layer's recall assumptions directly decide which signals can even be used — the two are tightly linked.

q: 轻量 ranker（light ranker）在多阶段推荐里的主要优化目标是什么？
options: 完全替代 re-ranking/slate 层的多样性控制
对最终少量候选做最精细的打分
高召回、低延迟，把候选量级从万级降到百级
只负责记录请求日志
why: 轻 ranker 是一个计算优化层，宁可保留可疑的好视频，也不要在这一层过早误杀。
why_en: The lightweight ranker is a high-recall, low-latency filter that shrinks the candidate set before the heavy ranker runs.
options_en: Fully replacing the diversity control done at the re-ranking/slate layer
Doing the finest-grained scoring on the last small batch of candidates
High recall, low latency, shrinking candidates from ten-thousands down to hundreds
Only logging requests
q_en: What is the light ranker's primary optimization target in a multi-stage recommender?
optionExplanations: 多样性控制是 reranking/slate 层的活，轻 ranker 不负责这个。
对少量候选做最精细打分是重 ranker 的工作，轻 ranker 追求的是速度不是精细。
轻 ranker 是计算优化层，用高召回、低延迟把候选量级从万级降到百级。
只记录请求日志是基础设施职责，不是轻 ranker 的优化目标。
optionExplanations_en: Diversity control belongs to the re-ranking/slate stage, not the light ranker.
Scoring a small candidate set with maximum precision is the heavy ranker's job — the light ranker optimizes for speed, not precision.
The light ranker is a compute-optimization layer aiming for high recall and low latency, cutting candidates from tens of thousands down to hundreds.
Just logging requests is an infrastructure concern, not what the light ranker optimizes for.
scenario: 候选生成给出约 1 万条视频，重 ranker 只吃得下几百条，这一层只有几十毫秒预算。
scenario_en: Candidate generation returns about ten thousand videos, the heavy ranker can only take a few hundred, and this stage has tens of milliseconds.

q: 重 ranker（heavy ranker）相比轻 ranker，主要多做了什么？
options: 用完整特征和更复杂的交互对少量候选精确评分
把候选量级从百级进一步扫描回全库规模
只返回一份固定的全站热门榜
只负责把候选结果写入缓存
why: 候选数被轻 ranker 降低后，重模型才有算力预算去用序列建模、交叉特征和多任务头追求排序质量。
why_en: The heavy ranker uses richer features and interactions to score a much smaller candidate set with higher accuracy.
options_en: Scoring a small set of candidates precisely using the full feature set and richer interactions
Scanning back up from hundreds of candidates to the whole catalog
Always returning one fixed platform-wide trending list
Only writing candidate results into a cache
q_en: Compared to the light ranker, what does the heavy ranker mainly add?
optionExplanations: 重 ranker 用完整特征和更复杂的交互，对轻 ranker 筛过的少量候选精确打分。
重 ranker 是在小候选集上做精细计算，不会反过来把候选量级扩回全库规模。
固定返回全站热门榜是没有排序模型的做法，和重 ranker 的职责相反。
把结果写入缓存是基础设施层的事，不是重 ranker 相比轻 ranker 多做的核心工作。
optionExplanations_en: The heavy ranker scores the small, pre-filtered candidate set precisely, using full features and richer interactions.
The heavy ranker works on a small candidate set — it doesn't scan back out to full-library scale.
Returning a fixed sitewide trending list is what you'd do with no ranking model at all, the opposite of the heavy ranker's job.
Writing results to cache is an infrastructure task, not the extra work that distinguishes the heavy ranker from the light one.
scenario: 轻排把候选从 1 万降到 500 条后，你还剩约 100ms 算力可以花在这 500 条上。
scenario_en: After the light ranker cuts ten thousand candidates to five hundred, you still have roughly 100 milliseconds of compute to spend on them.

q: re-ranking/slate 层在重 ranker 打完分之后还要额外处理什么？
options: 把所有候选全部丢弃，只保留人工挑选的视频
重新从零训练主排序模型
重新生成原始视频文件
按整体列表优化多样性并应用 value model
why: 单个视频的分数高不等于整份列表最优，reranker 要处理去重、多样性、新创作者探索和业务约束。
why_en: The reranker optimizes the whole slate for diversity, business constraints, and value beyond each item's individual score.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Scores[Item scores] --> Slate[Slate builder]
  Slate --> Diversity[Diversity]
  Slate --> Fresh[Freshness]
  Slate --> Creator[Creator constraints]
  Diversity --> Final[Final list]
  Fresh --> Final
  Creator --> Final
options_en: Discarding all candidates and keeping only a manually curated list
Retraining the main ranking model from scratch
Regenerating the original video files
Optimizing the whole list for diversity and applying the value model
q_en: After the heavy ranker scores candidates, what extra work does the re-ranking / slate layer still need to do?

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个预测头输出按业务权重汇总成一个排序分数的模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A value model combines several predicted signals into one business-weighted ranking score.

optionExplanations: 丢弃全部候选只留人工挑选会让系统失去可扩展性，不是 reranker 的做法。
reranker 不重新训练主排序模型，它是在已有分数基础上调整列表。
重新生成原始视频文件跟排序完全无关，那是内容处理层的事。
重 ranker 只顾单条打分，slate 层还要在列表整体层面处理去重、多样性和业务约束，两者分工不同。
optionExplanations_en: Discarding every candidate for a hand-picked list would throw away scalability — that's not what a reranker does.
The reranker doesn't retrain the main ranking model; it adjusts the list on top of scores that already exist.
Regenerating raw video files has nothing to do with ranking — that belongs to content processing.
The heavy ranker only scores items one at a time; the slate layer is the one handling dedup, diversity, and business constraints across the whole list — a different job.
scenario: 重 ranker 打完分，Top 20 里有 8 条来自同一创作者的相似视频，还要满足业务约束。
scenario_en: After heavy ranking, eight of the top twenty are near-duplicates from the same creator, and business constraints still have to hold.

q: 多阶段推荐架构（候选生成→轻排→重排→reranker）最主要的风险之一是什么？
options: 早期阶段漏掉的好候选，后面阶段无法恢复
多阶段架构在数学上一定比单阶段架构更无偏
多阶段架构不需要任何监控
多阶段架构会自动消除推荐反馈循环
why: 每个阶段都可能引入偏差和召回损失，所以需要单独监控每层的 recall 和分布，而不只是看最终指标。
why_en: A multi-stage recommender can permanently lose good items if early candidate generation or filtering misses them.
options_en: Good candidates missed by an early stage can never be recovered later
A multi-stage architecture is mathematically guaranteed to be less biased than a single-stage one
A multi-stage architecture needs no monitoring at all
A multi-stage architecture automatically eliminates recommendation feedback loops
q_en: What is one of the biggest risks of a multi-stage recommendation architecture (candidate generation → light ranking → heavy ranking → reranker)?
optionExplanations: 早期阶段没召回的好候选，后面阶段根本看不到，等于永久丢失。
多阶段架构不天然更无偏，每一层反而都可能引入新的偏差。
恰恰相反，每层都要单独监控 recall 和分布，不能只看最终指标。
多阶段架构不会自动消除反馈循环，热门内容照样可能被层层放大。
optionExplanations_en: A good candidate missed at an early stage is invisible to every later stage — that loss is permanent.
Multi-stage systems aren't inherently more unbiased; every stage can introduce its own new bias.
The opposite is true — each layer needs its own recall and distribution monitoring, not just a final-metric check.
Staging doesn't auto-eliminate feedback loops; popular content can still get amplified layer by layer.
scenario: 线上 A/B 里最终排序 NDCG 没变，但用户反馈说再也刷不到小众创作者了。
scenario_en: In the A/B test final-stage NDCG is flat, yet users report they never see niche creators any more.

q: 视频推荐训练数据中的 explicit feedback（显式反馈）包括哪些？（多选）
options: 点赞/点踩
订阅创作者
标记“不感兴趣”
用户从不主动表达的被动观看行为
why: 显式反馈质量高但很稀疏，大多数用户消费内容时并不会主动做出这些动作。
why_en: Explicit feedback includes likes, dislikes, subscriptions, and not-interested marks, but it is sparse compared to passive viewing.
options_en: Likes and dislikes
Subscribing to a creator
Marking a video 'not interested'
Passive watching that the user never actively expresses
q_en: Which of these count as explicit feedback in video-recommendation training data? (select all)
optionExplanations: 点赞/点踩是用户主动做出的偏好表态，属于典型的显式反馈。
订阅创作者是一次主动、持续性的偏好承诺，信号强但稀疏。
标记不感兴趣是用户主动排斥某类内容的表态，同样是显式反馈。
被动观看行为是从行为中推断出来的，属于隐式反馈而不是显式反馈。
optionExplanations_en: Likes/dislikes are an active, explicit statement of preference — the textbook definition of explicit feedback.
Subscribing to a creator is a deliberate, ongoing commitment of preference — strong but sparse.
Marking something 'not interested' is an active rejection of a content type, also explicit feedback.
Passive watching is inferred from behavior, which makes it implicit feedback, not explicit.
scenario: 你要给召回模型挑一批高精度但稀疏的监督信号，只算用户主动做出的动作。
scenario_en: You need high-precision but sparse supervision for the retrieval model, counting only actions the user deliberately takes.

q: 视频推荐训练数据中的 implicit feedback（隐式反馈）包括哪些？（多选）
options: 观看时长（绝对值和相对视频长度的比例）
点击历史
分享行为
观看后是否返回平台
why: 大多数用户不会显式评分，训练数据主要靠从行为中推断偏好；观看后离开平台是很强的隐式负信号。
why_en: Implicit feedback includes watch time, click history, sharing behavior, and whether the user returns to the platform afterward.
options_en: Watch time, both absolute and relative to video length
Click history
Sharing behavior
Whether the user returns to the platform after watching
q_en: Which of these count as implicit feedback in video-recommendation training data? (select all)
optionExplanations: 观看时长（绝对值和相对视频长度的比例）能反映用户对内容的实际投入程度。
点击历史记录了用户主动选择过哪些内容，是最基础的隐式信号。
分享行为说明用户认可到愿意推荐给别人，是更强的隐式信号。
观看后是否返回平台，是判断这次推荐有没有伤害长期留存的强隐式负信号。
optionExplanations_en: Watch duration, both absolute and relative to video length, reflects how invested the user actually was.
Click history records what a user actively chose to open — the most basic implicit signal.
Sharing shows the user liked something enough to pass it on — a stronger implicit signal.
Whether someone returns to the platform after watching is a strong implicit negative signal about whether that recommendation hurt retention.
scenario: 显式反馈只覆盖不到 1% 的曝光，你必须从被动行为里推断偏好来补足训练数据。
scenario_en: Explicit feedback covers under one percent of impressions, so you must infer preference from passive behavior to fill the training set.

scenario: 用户在 onboarding 阶段勾选了“我喜欢科技类视频”，但过去一个月的实际观看记录几乎全是烹饪视频。
q: 这种情况下，Up Next 推荐更应该信任哪个信号？
options: onboarding 时勾选的显式兴趣，因为是用户亲口说的
revealed preference：实际的观看和互动行为
两个信号完全随机取一个
只看用户的注册年龄
whenOtherWins: 新用户刚注册、还没有多少行为数据时，显式 onboarding 偏好仍然很有参考价值。
why: 用户常常说不清自己真正喜欢什么，显式兴趣和实际行为之间的差距可能很大，行为更能反映当下偏好。
why_en: Revealed behavioral preferences usually beat stated interests once enough interaction data has accumulated.
tradeoff: 显式表达的即时可得性 vs 实际行为反映真实偏好的准确性

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户实际行为中推断出的真实偏好，区别于用户口头表达的偏好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Revealed preference is the true preference inferred from what a user actually does, as opposed to what they say they like.

options_en: The explicit interest checked during onboarding, because the user stated it themselves
Revealed preference: the user's actual watching and interaction behavior
Pick randomly between the two signals
Only the user's account registration age
q_en: In this situation, which signal should Up Next trust more?
scenario_en: During onboarding the user checked "I like tech videos," but their actual watch history over the past month is almost entirely cooking videos.
optionExplanations: 用户嘴上说喜欢科技，不代表这就是当下真实偏好，尤其是一个月前随手勾选的。
revealed preference 看的是实际观看和互动行为，比一次性的自述更接近当下真实偏好。
两个信号完全随机选一个等于放弃判断，没有利用任何有效信息。
只看注册年龄和用户当下想看什么完全无关，不是一个有效信号。
optionExplanations_en: Saying you like tech during onboarding isn't the same as your actual preference right now, especially a month-old checkbox.
Revealed preference looks at real watching and interaction behavior, which tracks current taste far better than a one-time self-report.
Randomly picking between the two signals throws away useful information instead of using it.
Account registration age has nothing to do with what the user wants to watch right now.

q: Up Next 推荐可以用到的上下文数据包括哪些？（多选）
options: 用户当前正在观看的视频
最近的搜索 query
当前设备类型和一天中的时间
当前 session 内已经看过的视频序列
why: Up Next 强依赖当前意图，当前视频和会话内行为往往比长期画像更能解释用户接下来想看什么。
why_en: Up Next context includes the current video, recent search queries, device and time, and the session's watch sequence.
options_en: The video the user is currently watching
Recent search queries
Current device type and time of day
The sequence of videos already watched in this session
q_en: Which of these count as contextual data usable for Up Next recommendations? (select all)
optionExplanations: 当前正在看的视频最直接反映用户此刻的意图，是 Up Next 最强的上下文信号。
最近的搜索 query 透露了用户当下主动想找的内容方向。
设备类型和一天中的时间会影响用户当下想看的内容长短和类型。
本次 session 内已经看过的序列，能揭示用户这一路的兴趣演变。
optionExplanations_en: The video someone is watching right now is Up Next's strongest signal of immediate intent.
A recent search query reveals what the user is actively trying to find right now.
Device type and time of day shape what kind of content the user wants at this moment.
The sequence of videos already watched this session reveals how the user's interest is drifting in real time.
scenario: 用户长期画像偏科技，但此刻正在看旅行 vlog，Up Next 要抓当下这一次的意图。
scenario_en: The long-term profile says tech, but the user is watching a travel vlog right now, and Up Next has to catch this session's intent.

q: 标题、缩略图、音频、主题 embedding 这类视频内容特征的服务特点是什么？
options: 只能由人工逐条撰写
每次请求都必须重新从原始视频文件计算
在视频上传或编辑时计算一次，可以长期缓存
对排序完全没有帮助
why: 标题、描述、标签、缩略图、音频、转录和主题 embedding 相对静态，适合在上传时离线计算并缓存。
why_en: Video content features are mostly static and can be computed once at upload time, then cached for reuse.
options_en: Only written by hand
Recomputed from the raw video file on every single request
Computed once at upload or edit time and cached for a long time
Completely useless for ranking
scenario: 视频内容特征包含标题、描述、缩略图、音频和主题 embedding 等，在上传时就能拿到原始素材。
q_en: What is the serving characteristic of video content features like title, thumbnail, audio, and topic embedding?
scenario_en: Video content features include title, description, thumbnail, audio, and topic embedding, all available from the raw upload as soon as the video is uploaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

optionExplanations: 标题缩略图这些特征并不是只能人工逐条写，很多是自动提取的（音频/主题 embedding）。
每次请求都从原始视频重新计算的成本太高，也没必要，这类特征相对静态。
这类内容特征在上传或编辑时算一次就能长期缓存，不需要每次请求重算。
标题、缩略图等内容特征本身就是重要的排序输入，不是没用的信息。
optionExplanations_en: These features aren't purely hand-written — many, like audio or topic embeddings, are extracted automatically.
Recomputing from the raw video on every request is both expensive and unnecessary since these features are fairly static.
Content features like these can be computed once at upload or edit time and cached for a long time, no per-request recompute needed.
Title, thumbnail, and similar content features are actually useful ranking inputs, not dead weight.

q: 为什么视频的 engagement 特征（如累计观看量）要做年龄归一化，而不能直接比较原始计数？
options: 累计观看量数字永远无偏，不需要任何处理
新视频观看量天然少，直接比较会偏向老视频
归一化会把所有信号都清零
视频的上传时间根本无法被系统记录
why: 刚上传的视频天然观看量少，热门视频还会有反馈循环放大效应，原始计数会系统性误导排序。
why_en: Engagement features need age normalization because raw counts confound quality with how long a video has been live.
options_en: Raw view counts are always unbiased and need no processing
New videos naturally have fewer views, so a raw comparison favors older videos
Normalization zeroes out every signal
Upload time simply cannot be recorded by the system
q_en: Why do video engagement features (like cumulative view count) need age normalization instead of comparing raw counts directly?
optionExplanations: 累计观看量恰恰不是无偏的，越新的视频天然吃亏，越老的视频天然占便宜。
新视频上线时间短，累计观看量天然就少，直接比较会系统性偏向老视频。
归一化是按年龄调整数值，不是把所有信号清零，两者完全不同。
视频上传时间是系统记录的基本元数据，完全能被追踪到。
optionExplanations_en: Cumulative view counts are exactly not unbiased — newer videos are structurally disadvantaged, older ones structurally favored.
A new video simply hasn't had time to accumulate views, so comparing raw counts systematically favors older videos.
Normalization adjusts values for age; it doesn't zero out every signal — those are different things.
Upload time is basic metadata the system already records and can track.
scenario: 热榜里全是三年前的老视频，今天上传的新视频累计观看量天然只有几百。
scenario_en: The trending list is all three-year-old videos, because anything uploaded today has only a few hundred lifetime views.

scenario: 一条新视频刚发布 30 分钟，累计观看量还不高，但增长速度明显超过同类视频在同一时间窗口的平均水平。
q: 这种情况下，哪个特征更适合捕捉这条视频的早期潜力？
options: 视频 ID 数字的大小
视频当前的累计观看总量原始值
相对预期曲线的观看和互动增长速度
视频标题的字符长度
whenOtherWins: 如果比较的是发布时间窗口完全相同的一批视频，原始计数的偏差会小很多，可以直接比较。
why: 速度类特征能校正视频年龄带来的偏差，及时识别早期动量；原始观看总量会系统性偏向发布更久的视频。
why_en: Velocity relative to an expected growth curve is a better early-engagement signal than a raw view-count total.
tradeoff: 对早期动量的敏感度 vs 原始计数的简单直接
options_en: The magnitude of the video ID number
The video's current raw cumulative view count
View and engagement growth rate relative to an expected curve
The character length of the video title
q_en: In this situation, which feature better captures the video's early potential?
scenario_en: A video was published 30 minutes ago; its cumulative view count is still low, but its growth rate is clearly outpacing the average for similar videos in the same time window.
optionExplanations: 视频 ID 只是一个自增编号，和内容受欢迎程度没有任何关系。
原始累计观看总量对刚发布 30 分钟的视频天然很小，看不出早期动量。
相对预期曲线的增长速度能校正视频年龄偏差，及时识别真正跑出来的早期动量。
标题字符长度是文本属性，不能反映观看和互动的增长趋势。
optionExplanations_en: A video ID is just an auto-incrementing number with no relationship to how well content is performing.
Raw cumulative view count is naturally tiny 30 minutes after upload, so it can't reveal early momentum.
Growth velocity relative to the expected curve corrects for video age and catches genuine early momentum in time.
Title character length is a text attribute that says nothing about watch or engagement growth.

q: 长期用户画像（profile features）和当前 session 行为特征的核心区别是什么？
options: session 行为特征只能离线批量计算
两者携带的信息完全相同，只是存储的位置不一样而已
长期画像反映稳定偏好，session 行为反映此刻意图
长期画像一旦生成就永远不需要更新
why: 用户可能长期喜欢科技内容，但当前 session 正在看旅行视频；推荐要结合稳定偏好和此刻意图。
why_en: Long-term user profiles capture stable taste, while session behavior captures the user's immediate intent.
tradeoff: 长期偏好的稳定代表性 vs 会话行为的即时相关性
options_en: Session behavior features can only be computed offline in batch
The two carry exactly the same information; they just live in different storage locations
A long-term profile reflects stable preference, while session behavior reflects intent right now
A long-term profile never needs to be updated once it's built
q_en: What is the core difference between a long-term user profile (profile features) and current-session behavior features?
optionExplanations: session 行为特征恰恰要接近实时更新，才能跟上用户此刻的兴趣变化。
两者携带的信息完全不同：一个是稳定偏好，一个是此刻意图，不只是存储位置差异。
长期画像反映稳定偏好，session 行为反映此刻意图，两者时间尺度不同、要结合使用。
长期画像会随新行为持续更新，不是生成后就永久固定不变。
optionExplanations_en: Session behavior features need to update close to real time to keep up with shifting intent, not just batch offline.
The two carry genuinely different information — stable preference versus right-now intent — not just a storage-location difference.
Long-term profiles capture stable preference while session behavior captures right-now intent; they operate on different timescales and should be combined.
Long-term profiles keep getting updated as new behavior comes in — they aren't frozen once generated.
scenario: 用户长期画像是科技类，但这个 session 已经连看 4 个露营视频，要选用哪组特征。
scenario_en: The profile says tech, but this session already has four camping videos in a row, and you must decide which feature group to lean on.

scenario: 轻 ranker 要在毫秒级处理海量候选，重 ranker 则可以承担更贵的计算来追求质量。两者都要用到用户最近观看历史。
q: 轻 ranker 和重 ranker 分别应该如何编码这份观看历史？
options: 轻 ranker 用历史 embedding 均值聚合，重 ranker 用完整序列建模
轻 ranker 反过来用完整 Transformer，重 ranker 只用简单均值聚合
两个阶段处理历史时都完全不使用任何观看记录
两个阶段编码历史时都只依赖用户的注册年龄字段
whenOtherWins: 如果历史很短且候选数量本来就很少，两个阶段都可以用更复杂的序列编码而不担心延迟。
why: 宽漏斗（轻 ranker）用便宜的聚合特征换速度，窄漏斗（重 ranker）才有算力预算去用序列模型捕捉顺序和上下文。
why_en: Light rankers can use cheap aggregated history embeddings, while heavy rankers can afford full sequence modeling.
tradeoff: 编码复杂度带来的表达力 vs 阶段各自的延迟预算
options_en: The light ranker uses a mean-pooled history embedding, while the heavy ranker models the full sequence
The light ranker instead uses a full Transformer, while the heavy ranker just does simple mean pooling
Neither stage uses any watch-history records at all when encoding history
Both stages rely only on the user's account registration-age field when encoding history
q_en: How should the light ranker and heavy ranker each encode this watch history?
scenario_en: The light ranker has to process a huge candidate set at millisecond-level latency, while the heavy ranker can afford more expensive computation for quality. Both stages need the user's recent watch history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于注意力机制建模序列的神经网络架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer is a neural network architecture that models sequences using attention.

optionExplanations: 轻 ranker 用均值聚合换速度，重 ranker 才有算力预算跑完整序列建模捕捉顺序。
反过来做的话轻 ranker 会因为 Transformer 太贵拖垮延迟，重 ranker 也白白浪费了算力预算。
两阶段都完全不用观看记录，就丢掉了个性化推荐最核心的行为信号。
注册年龄跟这一刻想看什么几乎无关，不能替代真实的观看历史。
optionExplanations_en: The light ranker mean-pools history embeddings for speed, while the heavy ranker has the compute budget to run full sequence modeling.
Doing it backwards would blow the light ranker's latency budget with a full Transformer, while wasting the heavy ranker's compute on simple pooling.
Skipping watch history entirely at both stages throws away the core behavioral signal personalization depends on.
Registration age says almost nothing about what someone wants to watch right now, so it can't substitute for real watch history.

scenario: 推荐系统第一次上线，团队还没有任何线上效果数据，需要一个可比较的基线（baseline）。
q: 这种情况下，合理的 baseline 应该是什么？
options: 随机混合各 generator 的输出，或用简单协同过滤
直接上线目前能训练出的最大 Transformer 模型，且不设对照组
由人工每天手动挑选固定 5 个视频
只按视频上传时间倒序排列
why: 基线给复杂系统一个比较起点，也能提前发现简单方法是否已经足够强，是否值得投入更复杂的模型。
why_en: A recommender baseline can be a random blend of generator outputs or a simple collaborative-filtering approach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据相似用户或相似物品的历史行为来做推荐的经典方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends items based on the behavior of similar users or similar items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于注意力机制建模序列的神经网络架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer is a neural network architecture that models sequences using attention.

options_en: A random blend of generator outputs, or a simple collaborative-filtering approach
Ship the largest Transformer the team can train right away, with no control group
Have a human manually curate a fixed five videos every day
Sort purely by upload time, most recent first
tradeoff: 简单基线建立可比较起点 vs 直接上线复杂模型却无从验证效果的风险
whenOtherWins: 如果团队已经有相邻产品线的历史基线数据可以复用，重新构建这一步可以跳过。
q_en: In this situation, what would a reasonable baseline be?
scenario_en: The recommendation system is launching for the first time; the team has no online performance data yet and needs a comparable baseline.
optionExplanations: 随机混合各路 generator 输出，或用简单协同过滤，成本低又能给复杂系统一个真实的比较起点。
不设对照组直接上线最大模型，事后根本无法判断这套复杂系统是不是真的比基线好。
人工每天手动选 5 个视频没法覆盖十亿级用户规模，也不是可复用的系统性方案。
纯按上传时间倒序完全忽略个性化信号，作为基线过于弱，参考价值有限。
optionExplanations_en: A random blend of generator outputs or simple collaborative filtering is cheap and gives the complex system a real point of comparison.
Shipping the biggest model with no control group leaves no way to tell afterward whether the complex system actually beat a baseline.
Hand-picking five videos a day can't scale to a billion users and isn't a repeatable system-level approach.
Sorting purely by upload time ignores personalization entirely, making it too weak a baseline to be very informative.

q: embedding-based candidate generator 常用的训练结构是什么？
options: 双塔（two-tower）模型 + triplet loss
单一的 softmax 多分类器
Isolation forest 是一种异常检测模型
Platt scaling 校准方法
why: 用户塔和视频塔各自产出向量，训练时让正样本视频更近、负样本视频更远，再把向量存入向量库做召回。
why_en: Embedding candidate generators are typically trained with a two-tower architecture using a triplet or contrastive objective.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  User[User tower] --> U[User vector]
  Video[Video tower] --> V[Video vector]
  U --> Loss[Contrastive loss]
  V --> Loss
  V --> Index[Vector index]
  U --> Search[ANN search]

termDefinitions.meaning: 召回模型结构，用户和物品分别经过独立的编码塔产生可比较的向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes the user and the item with separate towers into comparable vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对比学习损失函数，让正样本比负样本更接近锚点至少一个 margin。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Triplet loss pulls a positive example closer to the anchor than a negative example by at least a margin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种通过随机切分快速孤立异常点的异常检测算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isolation forest is an anomaly-detection algorithm that isolates outliers via random partitioning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型原始分数校准成概率的常用方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling calibrates raw model scores into probabilities.

options_en: A two-tower model with a triplet or contrastive loss
A single softmax multi-class classifier
Isolation forest, which is a type of anomaly-detection model
Platt scaling calibration
scenario: 候选生成层要从上亿视频里快速检索出语义相关的候选，而不是逐条计算相似度。
q_en: What training architecture is commonly used for embedding-based candidate generators?
scenario_en: The candidate-generation layer needs to quickly retrieve semantically relevant candidates from hundreds of millions of videos, rather than computing similarity one by one.
optionExplanations: 用户塔和视频塔各自编码成向量，用 triplet loss 拉近正样本、推远负样本，训练完向量可以直接存进向量库做检索。
单一 softmax 多分类器要对十亿级候选做归一化，计算量和类别数一起爆炸，不适合这种规模的检索。
Isolation forest 是异常检测算法，用来隔离离群点，和学习用户-视频相似度的检索任务不是一回事。
Platt scaling 是把模型原始分数校准成概率的方法，用在训练完之后，不是训练检索模型本身的结构。
optionExplanations_en: The user and video towers each encode a vector, and triplet loss pulls positives closer while pushing negatives away, producing vectors you can drop straight into a vector index.
A single softmax classifier would need to normalize over a billion-scale candidate set, exploding in compute as classes grow — not built for this scale.
Isolation forest is an anomaly-detection algorithm for isolating outliers, a completely different problem from learning user-video similarity.
Platt scaling calibrates raw scores into probabilities after training — it's not the architecture used to train a retrieval model.

scenario: 你要向面试官解释 user-video two-tower candidate generator 训练时用的这条 triplet loss 公式。
q: 下面这段公式在训练中起什么作用？
codeSample: L = max(0, margin + d(user, positive_video) - d(user, negative_video))
options: 校准 harmful content 的判定阈值
计算 NDCG 排序指标
让用户向量更接近正样本视频、更远离负样本视频
平滑小分母导致的除零错误
whenOtherWins: 如果 batch 很大且能取 in-batch negatives，InfoNCE 这类对比损失通常比逐三元组的 triplet loss 更高效。
why: triplet loss 要求正样本到用户的距离比负样本小至少一个 margin；训练时偏向采样“难负样本”能让模型学得更细。
why_en: The triplet loss pulls the user embedding closer to positive videos than to negative videos by at least a margin.
tradeoff: 逐三元组采样的可控性 vs in-batch negative 的训练效率

termDefinitions.meaning: triplet loss 中要求正负样本距离至少相差的间隔值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The margin is the minimum required gap between the positive and negative distances in a triplet loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 违规或有害内容，通常由独立的信任与安全模型判定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Harmful content is policy-violating material, usually judged by a separate trust-and-safety model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折扣累积增益，一种衡量排序质量、对靠前位置加权更高的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG is a ranking-quality metric that gives more weight to correctly-ordered items near the top.

termDefinitions.meaning: 召回模型结构，用户和物品分别经过独立的编码塔产生可比较的向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes the user and the item with separate towers into comparable vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对比学习损失函数，让正样本比负样本更接近锚点至少一个 margin。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Triplet loss pulls a positive example closer to the anchor than a negative example by at least a margin.

options_en: Calibrating the threshold for flagging harmful content
Computing the NDCG ranking metric
Pulling the user embedding closer to positive videos and farther from negative ones
Smoothing out a divide-by-zero error from a small denominator
q_en: What does this formula do during training?
scenario_en: You need to explain to the interviewer what this triplet-loss formula does when training the user-video two-tower candidate generator.
optionExplanations: 校准 harmful content 阈值是内容安全的事，跟这条 triplet loss 公式要优化的目标无关。
NDCG 是评估排序质量的离线指标，不是训练时用来更新参数的损失函数。
这条公式让用户向量向正样本视频靠拢、远离负样本视频，训练出能直接做相似度检索的向量空间。
平滑除零错误是数值稳定性技巧，不是 triplet loss 这类对比学习公式要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Calibrating a harmful-content threshold is a trust-and-safety task, unrelated to what this triplet loss formula is optimizing.
NDCG is an offline ranking-quality metric, not a loss function used to update parameters during training.
This formula pulls the user vector toward positive-sample videos and away from negative ones, training a vector space usable directly for similarity search.
Smoothing a divide-by-zero error is a numerical-stability trick, not something a contrastive loss like triplet loss is solving.

q: 视频召回模型训练中的 hard negative（难负样本）指的是什么？
options: 没有生成 embedding 的视频
和用户兴趣完全无关的随机冷门视频
用户已经完整看完并点赞的视频
模型认为用户可能喜欢，但用户没有给出正反馈的视频
why: 难负样本比随机负样本更接近决策边界，能教会模型区分“看起来相似但其实不合适”的视频。
why_en: Hard negatives are plausible-looking videos the user did not engage with, which makes retrieval training sharper than using random negatives.
options_en: A video that has no embedding generated for it
A random, completely irrelevant, obscure video
A video the user already watched in full and liked
A video the model thinks the user might like, but got no positive feedback on
q_en: What does a 'hard negative' mean when training a video retrieval model?

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型认为用户可能喜欢、但用户实际没有给出正反馈的负样本，比随机负样本更接近决策边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard negative is a plausible-looking item the user did not engage with, sitting closer to the decision boundary than a random negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

optionExplanations: 系统还没给它算出 embedding、进不了候选池的视频，跟难负样本是两回事。
和用户兴趣完全不沾边、随机抽到的冷门视频，是普通负样本而不是难负样本。
用户已经完整看完、还主动点了赞的视频，是正样本，不是负样本。
这正是难负样本的定义：模型判断它可能被喜欢，但实际没换来正向反馈，逼模型学会区分相似却不合适的内容。
optionExplanations_en: A video the system hasn't computed an embedding for yet can't even enter the candidate pool — that's not what a hard negative is.
A random, obscure video with nothing to do with the user's interests is an easy negative, not a hard one.
A video the user already watched in full and liked is a positive sample, not a negative one.

This is exactly the definition of a hard negative: the model judged it likely to be liked, but got no real positive signal back, forcing it to learn the line between similar-looking and actually right.
scenario: 双塔召回用随机负样本训练后，线上召回的视频看起来相关，用户却几乎不点。
scenario_en: After training the two-tower retriever with random negatives, the recalled videos look relevant online but users barely click them.

scenario: 轻 ranker 要在 CPU 上以亚毫秒延迟处理海量候选，团队目前 GPU 资源紧张。
q: 轻 ranker 更适合选择下面哪种模型？
options: 人工逐条审核每个候选
和重 ranker 一样规模的完整 Transformer
从重 ranker 蒸馏出来的 skinny MLP
GBDT / LightGBM、XGBoost 这类树模型
whenOtherWins: 如果已经有从重 ranker 蒸馏好的小型 MLP，且分类特征的 embedding 足够丰富，skinny MLP 也可能是更优选择。
why: GBDT 对结构化、聚合类特征表现很强，能在 CPU 上以亚毫秒延迟运行，适合高吞吐的过滤层。
why_en: A GBDT is a practical light ranker because it runs fast on CPU and performs strongly on tabular recommendation features.
tradeoff: GBDT 的 CPU 低延迟 vs Transformer 的表达力和 GPU 依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升决策树，把多棵弱决策树顺序叠加训练的树模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GBDT is a gradient boosted decision tree, an ensemble of weak trees trained sequentially.

termDefinitions.meaning: 参数量很小、专为低延迟场景设计的多层感知机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skinny MLP is a small-parameter multi-layer perceptron designed for low-latency serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于注意力机制建模序列的神经网络架构，算力需求远高于树模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer is an attention-based architecture that needs far more compute than a tree model.

options_en: Manual human review of every candidate
A full-size Transformer as large as the heavy ranker
A skinny MLP distilled from the heavy ranker
A tree model such as GBDT, LightGBM, or XGBoost
q_en: Which kind of model best fits the light ranker here?
scenario_en: The light ranker must process a huge candidate set on CPU at sub-millisecond latency, and the team is currently short on GPU capacity.
optionExplanations: 人工逐条审核没法在亚毫秒延迟里处理海量候选，规模上就不成立。
和重 ranker 同规模的完整 Transformer 在 CPU 上跑不进亚毫秒延迟，GPU 资源又紧张。
蒸馏出的 skinny MLP 也是可行选项，但需要先有训练好的重 ranker 和足够丰富的类别 embedding。
树模型吃得动这类聚合统计特征，纯 CPU 也能跑进亚毫秒，刚好卡住轻 ranker 的延迟线又不用抢 GPU。
optionExplanations_en: Manual review can't process a huge candidate pool at sub-millisecond latency — it doesn't work at this scale at all.
A full-size Transformer matching the heavy ranker won't hit sub-millisecond latency on CPU, and GPU capacity is tight anyway.
A distilled skinny MLP is workable too, but it needs a trained heavy ranker and rich categorical embeddings to distill from first.
Tree models handle these aggregated stats features well and run sub-millisecond on plain CPU, hitting the light ranker's latency line without competing for GPU.

q: 如果重 ranker 只用一个简单 MLP 把所有稀疏和稠密特征直接拼接后输入，主要局限是什么？
options: 会自动处理好展示位置带来的偏差
无法处理任何数值型特征

termDefinitions.meaning: 修正“展示位置越靠前越容易被点击”这一偏差的训练项。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling calibrates raw model scores into probabilities as a post-training step, not a training loss.

options_en: Computing the takedown threshold for harmful content
The vector reconstruction error of matrix factorization
Post-training Platt-scaling score calibration
A multitask loss: primary objective + auxiliary tasks + position-bias correction
q_en: What does this pseudocode describe?

矩阵分解的重构误差是另一类模型的目标函数，不是这里多目标 loss 组合的内容。
Platt scaling 是训练完之后校准分数用的，不是训练时优化的 loss 组成部分。
这段 loss 把主要 engagement 目标、辅助任务信号和位置偏差修正项加权组合在一起联合训练。

Matrix-factorization reconstruction error is the objective for a different kind of model, not what this multi-objective loss combines.

This loss jointly weights the main engagement objective, auxiliary task signals, and a position-bias correction term.

q: 为什么推荐训练要专门处理 position bias（位置偏差）？
options: 所有未被展示的视频都应该被当作明确的负反馈
用户只反馈被展示且靠前的视频，日志受旧系统影响
展示位置对点击行为完全没有影响
训练数据本身天然是反事实、无偏的
why: 不修正的话，新模型会学习去逼近旧系统的曝光模式，而不是学习真实的用户偏好。
why_en: Position bias exists because users only react to items that were shown, and higher-ranked items get more attention.
options_en: Every video that was never shown should be treated as a definite negative
Users only give feedback on items shown near the top, so logs reflect the old ranking system
Display position has no effect at all on click behavior
Training data is inherently counterfactual and unbiased
q_en: Why does recommendation training need to specifically correct for position bias?

termDefinitions.meaning: 展示位置越靠前的内容越容易被点击，导致训练日志系统性偏向旧系统的排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is the tendency for higher-ranked items to get more clicks, which skews training logs toward the old ranking system.

optionExplanations: 把所有未展示视频都当明确负反馈是常见误区——没展示只是没机会被看到，不代表用户不喜欢。
用户只能对被展示、且往往是排得靠前的视频给出反馈，训练日志因此带着旧排序系统的曝光偏差。
展示位置对点击行为影响很大，越靠前越容易被点，这正是需要修正的原因。
训练数据来自旧系统的真实展示记录，天然带着旧排序的偏差，并不是反事实、无偏的。
optionExplanations_en: Treating every unshown video as an explicit negative is a common misconception — not being shown just means no chance to be seen, not dislike.
Users can only react to videos that were actually shown, usually near the top, so training logs inherit the old system's exposure bias.
Position has a big effect on clicks — items ranked higher get clicked more, which is exactly why it needs correcting.
Training data comes from the old system's real exposure record, so it carries that system's bias — it's not counterfactual or unbiased on its own.
scenario: 训练日志全部来自旧排序系统，日志里第 1 位的点击率是第 10 位的 5 倍。
scenario_en: All training logs come from the old ranker, where position one gets five times the click rate of position ten.

scenario: 重 ranker 计算成本很高，但整套系统已经拆成多阶段架构，且展示预算只有约 250ms。
q: 哪些计算最应该挪到离线预计算或缓存，而不是放进在线路径？
options: 视频 embedding、慢变化的用户 embedding、候选生成结果
每次请求都要对候选池里的每一条视频重新执行一遍完整特征编码计算
所有历史 A/B 实验的结果记录
由人工对每个候选逐条打分
whenOtherWins: 如果用户兴趣会在分钟级快速变化，用户侧缓存就需要更短的 TTL，或改为支持在线增量更新。
why: 离线预计算和缓存把大部分稳定的计算移出 250ms 在线路径，在线只处理当前上下文和少量候选。
why_en: Video embeddings, slow-changing user embeddings, and candidate-generation results should be precomputed or cached to meet the latency budget.
tradeoff: 离线缓存带来的低延迟 vs 缓存数据可能出现的过期滞后
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Video[Video embeddings] --> Cache[Offline cache]
  User[User embeddings] --> Cache
  Gen[Generator results] --> Cache
  Cache --> Online[Fast online path]
  Context[Live context] --> Online
options_en: Video embeddings, slow-changing user embeddings, and candidate-generation results
Fully re-running the whole feature-encoding computation from scratch for every video in the pool on every single request
The recorded results of every historical A/B experiment
Having a human score every candidate one by one
q_en: Which computations should move to offline precompute or caching, rather than sitting on the online path?
scenario_en: The heavy ranker is expensive to run, but the system is already split into multiple stages, and the serving budget is only about 250ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组，对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into groups to compare the real-world effect of different versions.

optionExplanations: 视频 embedding、慢变化的用户 embedding、候选生成结果都是变化慢的稳定计算，适合提前算好缓存，只留当前上下文在线处理。
每次请求都对全库重新编码会让在线延迟远超 250ms 预算，这正是需要挪去离线的计算。
历史 A/B 实验结果是评估产出，不是候选打分需要的数据，跟这里要缓存的对象无关。
人工对每个候选逐条打分既无法覆盖十亿级候选，也做不到 250ms 内完成，不是可行方案。
optionExplanations_en: Video embeddings, slow-changing user embeddings, and candidate-generation results are all stable, slow-moving computations, so precomputing and caching them leaves only live context on the online path.
Re-encoding the entire library from scratch on every request blows the 250ms budget — that's exactly the kind of work that needs to move offline.
Historical A/B results are evaluation output, not data candidate scoring needs, so they're unrelated to what should be cached here.
Having a human score every candidate can't cover a billion-scale pool or finish within 250ms, so it isn't a workable option.

q: 像 Bytedance Monolith 这类系统代表的技术方向是什么？
options: 只是一套内容审核规则库
只做离线年度训练，不做任何在线更新
完全替代所有的排序模型
在线更新 embedding，快速吸收新行为
why: 实时推荐要快速吸收新的用户行为，在线高效更新 embedding 是复杂度更高但适应性更强的方向。
why_en: Monolith-like systems point toward efficient online embedding updates so recommendations adapt quickly to new behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 字节跳动提出的实时推荐系统，支持在线高效更新 embedding 表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Monolith is a real-time recommendation system from ByteDance that supports efficient online embedding-table updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实体映射成一个稠密向量，向量距离反映相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps an entity to a dense vector whose distance reflects similarity.

options_en: Just being a set of content-moderation rules
Only running offline training once a year, with no online updates at all
Fully replacing every ranking model
Updating embeddings online to absorb new behavior fast
q_en: What technical direction do systems like ByteDance's Monolith represent?
optionExplanations: 内容审核规则库是信任与安全系统，跟在线更新 embedding 的推荐技术方向不是一回事。
只做离线年度训练完全跟不上用户行为变化，这正是 Monolith 这类系统要解决的反面问题。
在线 embedding 更新是排序模型的一个组件升级，不会替代掉整套排序模型体系。
Monolith 这类系统让 embedding 表跟着新行为流式更新，几乎不用等下一轮离线训练，代价是工程实现更复杂。
optionExplanations_en: A content-moderation rule library is a trust-and-safety system, unrelated to online embedding updates as a recsys direction.
Training only once a year offline can't keep up with shifting user behavior — that's exactly the opposite problem systems like Monolith solve.
Online embedding updates upgrade one component of the ranking stack; they don't replace the whole ranking model system.
Systems like Monolith stream-update the embedding tables as new behavior arrives, barely waiting on the next offline training round, at the cost of more engineering complexity.
scenario: 热点事件视频 10 分钟内爆火，天级批量训练出的 embedding 完全跟不上。
scenario_en: A breaking-news video blows up within ten minutes, and embeddings trained in a daily batch simply cannot keep up.

q: 视频推荐系统的 serving 优化手段可以包括哪些？（多选）
options: 模型量化降低内存占用
用 GPU/TPU 提高吞吐
对候选结果和 embedding 做缓存
取消所有延迟监控
why: 这些优化帮助系统在排序质量和 250ms 延迟预算之间取得折中，延迟和错误率仍然要持续监控。
why_en: Serving optimizations include quantization, hardware accelerators, and caching, while latency monitoring must still continue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重压缩到更低精度以节省内存、提高推理速度的技术。

termDefinitions.meaning: 专用于并行矩阵运算的加速硬件，能提升模型 serving 的吞吐量。

options_en: Quantization to shrink model memory footprint
Using GPUs/TPUs to raise serving throughput
Caching candidate results and embeddings
Turning off all latency monitoring
q_en: What serving optimizations can a video recommendation system use? (select all)
optionExplanations: 模型量化把权重压缩成更低精度，降低内存占用和推理耗时。
用 GPU/TPU 提高并行吞吐，能在同样延迟预算里处理更多候选。

取消延迟监控只会让系统在出问题时毫无察觉，是纯粹的负优化，不是优化手段。
optionExplanations_en: Model quantization compresses weights to lower precision, cutting memory footprint and inference time.
Using GPU/TPU raises parallel throughput, letting the system handle more candidates within the same latency budget.
Caching candidate results and embeddings avoids repeated computation, directly cutting time off the online path.
Removing latency monitoring just means problems go unnoticed — that's a pure regression, not an optimization.

q: 视频推荐的离线评估应该同时覆盖哪些层面，而不是只看最终排序指标？
options: 各预测头质量、排序指标、多样性、召回率
只看模型最终输出的 accuracy
只看训练过程中的 loss 曲线
只看模型文件的大小
why: 多阶段系统里每一层都可能失败，只看最终 ranker 指标会掩盖候选生成阶段的召回问题和 slate 多样性问题。
why_en: Offline recommendation evaluation should cover per-head quality, ranking metrics, diversity, and candidate-generator recall.
options_en: Per-head quality, ranking metrics, diversity, and candidate recall
Only the model's final output accuracy
Only the training loss curve
Only the size of the model file
q_en: What should offline evaluation for video recommendations cover, instead of only looking at the final ranking metric?
optionExplanations: 多阶段系统每一层都可能出问题，只看最终排序指标会漏掉候选生成召回不足或 slate 缺乏多样性这类上游问题。
只看最终 accuracy 是单一指标，看不出问题出在召回层还是排序层，也看不出多样性有没有崩。
训练 loss 曲线只反映拟合过程，不代表线上排序质量或多样性表现。
模型文件大小是工程指标，跟推荐效果好不好没有直接关系。
optionExplanations_en: Every layer in a multi-stage system can fail on its own, so looking only at the final ranking metric hides upstream problems like weak recall or a lack of slate diversity.
Final accuracy alone is a single number that can't tell you whether the problem is in recall, ranking, or diversity collapse.
The training loss curve only reflects how well the model fit, not online ranking quality or diversity.
Model file size is an engineering metric with no direct bearing on how good the recommendations actually are.
scenario: 线上 A/B 掉了，可离线的最终排序 NDCG 却是涨的，你要定位是哪一层出了问题。
scenario_en: The online A/B is down while offline final-stage NDCG is up, and you need to find which stage actually broke.

q: 视频推荐可以用哪些离线排序相关指标？（多选）
options: NDCG
MAP
precision/recall
推荐结果的多样性和创作者覆盖度
why: 相关性指标衡量排序本身的质量，多样性和 creator coverage 则反映 slate 和创作者生态是否健康。
why_en: Video recommendation evaluation uses ranking metrics like NDCG, MAP, and precision/recall, plus diversity and creator coverage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均精度均值，衡量排序结果整体精确率的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAP, mean average precision, summarizes ranking precision across recall levels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确率衡量推荐结果中相关内容的比例，召回率衡量真正相关的内容有多少被找出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision measures how much of what was recommended is relevant, while recall measures how much of what is relevant was actually retrieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对靠前位置加权更高的排序质量指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG, Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain, is a ranking-quality metric that weights correct order near the top more heavily.

options_en: NDCG
MAP
Precision/recall
Diversity of recommendations and creator coverage
q_en: Which offline ranking-related metrics can video recommendations use? (select all)
optionExplanations: NDCG 按位置加权衡量整体排序质量，位置越靠前权重越大。
MAP 衡量多个相关结果的平均排序精度，适合有多个正确答案的场景。
precision/recall 分别看结果里有多少是相关的、相关结果里又召回了多少。
多样性和创作者覆盖度看的是 slate 是否单一同质、是否只集中曝光头部创作者。
optionExplanations_en: NDCG position-weights ranking quality, giving higher-ranked correct items more credit.
MAP measures average precision across multiple relevant results, suited to cases with more than one right answer.
Precision and recall separately check how many returned results are relevant and how many relevant items got surfaced at all.
Diversity and creator coverage check whether the slate is homogeneous or over-concentrated on a handful of top creators.
scenario: 上线前只能用离线日志判断新 ranker 是否更好，还要确认它没有把 slate 做窄。
scenario_en: Before launch you can only judge the new ranker from offline logs, and you also need proof it did not narrow the slate.

scenario: 你想评估某个 candidate generator 是否漏掉了本该召回的好视频。
q: 评估这类召回率时最大的难点是什么？
options: 需要无偏或更广的候选参考集，否则只看到已召回窗口
ranker 会自动帮你恢复被漏掉的候选
只看点击率就足够评估召回质量
这种评估在技术上完全无法进行
whenOtherWins: 如果视频目录本身很小，可以全量枚举，generator 召回率评估会简单很多。
why: 召回器漏掉的视频不会进入后续排序，因此评估要靠探索流量、近似全量枚举或窗口外样本构造参考。
why_en: Candidate-generator recall needs an unbiased or broader reference set, because downstream rankers cannot recover items that were never retrieved.
tradeoff: 评估的无偏性 vs 构造参考集所需的探索流量成本
options_en: It needs an unbiased or broader reference set, or you only see what was already retrieved
The ranker will automatically recover any candidates that were missed
Click-through rate alone is enough to evaluate recall quality
This kind of evaluation is simply impossible to run
q_en: What is the biggest difficulty in evaluating this kind of recall?
scenario_en: You want to evaluate whether a candidate generator is missing good videos it should have retrieved.
optionExplanations: 召回率要看漏掉了多少好视频，必须靠探索流量或近似全量枚举建一份更广的参考集，否则只能看到已召回窗口内的结果。
ranker 只能给召回到的候选打分，召不到的视频它根本看不到，不可能替你把漏掉的候选找回来。
只看点击率反映不了召回率，点击率高低跟召没召到全部好视频是两件事。
这种评估确实更难，但可以用探索流量或窗口外样本构造参考集，并非技术上做不到。
optionExplanations_en: Recall means measuring how much good content got missed, which needs an unbiased or broader reference set built from exploration traffic or near-full enumeration — otherwise you only ever see inside the already-recalled window.
The ranker can only score candidates it received; it never sees what wasn't recalled, so it can't recover missed candidates for you.
CTR alone doesn't reveal recall — a high click rate says nothing about whether good videos were missed entirely.
This kind of evaluation is harder, not impossible — exploration traffic or out-of-window samples can build a usable reference set.

q: 视频推荐系统线上评估的 gold standard 是什么？
options: A/B testing，对照分组比较业务和系统指标
只看离线的 NDCG 排序质量分数高低
只询问模型开发者本人的主观判断
只在训练集上重新跑一遍评估流程
why: 推荐的真正价值由用户的真实行为决定，A/B 测试能验证离线的改进是否真正转化为观看、留存和满意度的提升。
why_en: A/B testing is the gold standard for online recommendation evaluation because it measures real user behavior against a control group.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Users[Users] -->|randomize| Control[Control: current model]
  Users -->|randomize| Treatment[Treatment: new model]
  Control --> Compare[Compare metrics]
  Treatment --> Compare

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组，对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into groups to compare the real-world effect of different versions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对靠前位置加权更高的排序质量指标，属于离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG, Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain, is an offline ranking-quality metric that weights top positions more heavily.

options_en: A/B testing on real control and treatment groups
Only look at how high or low the offline NDCG ranking score is
Only ask the model developer's own subjective opinion
Only rerun the evaluation process on the training set
q_en: What is the gold standard for online evaluation of a video recommendation system?
optionExplanations: A/B testing 靠真实用户的对照实验直接验证效果，是能确认离线改进真正转化为业务价值的黄金标准。
离线 NDCG 只能反映历史数据上的排序质量，不能保证这些改进在真实用户身上一样成立。
只问开发者主观判断没有对照，容易受个人偏好和确认偏误影响，不算可靠证据。
只在训练集上重新评估拿到的还是模型已经见过的数据表现，看不出真实泛化效果。
optionExplanations_en: A/B testing validates impact directly through a real controlled experiment on users, making it the gold standard for confirming offline gains actually translate to business value.
Offline NDCG only reflects ranking quality on historical data — it doesn't guarantee the same gains hold for real users.
Asking a developer's subjective opinion has no control group and is easily swayed by personal bias or confirmation bias, so it isn't reliable evidence.
Re-evaluating only on the training set still measures data the model has already seen, which says nothing about real generalization.
scenario: 离线 NDCG 涨了 2%，但你无法确定它会不会转化成真实的观看时长和留存。
scenario_en: Offline NDCG is up two percent, but you cannot tell whether that turns into real watch time and retention.

q: 视频推荐的 A/B 实验应该同时跟踪哪些指标？（多选）

return visit rate 和长期 engagement 趋势
negative feedback / 用户调研反馈
latency、throughput、error rate

why_en: Recommendation A/B tests should track engagement, long-term retention, user-experience feedback, and system-health metrics together.
options_en: Session watch time
Return visit rate and long-term engagement trends
Negative feedback and survey responses
Latency, throughput, and error rate
q_en: What metrics should a video recommendation A/B test track at the same time? (select all)

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组，对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into groups to compare the real-world effect of different versions.

optionExplanations: session watch time 直接反映这次会话里用户实际投入了多少时间。
return visit rate 和长期 engagement 趋势能看出这次改动是不是只带来短期新鲜感。
negative feedback 和用户调研反馈能捕捉指标之外的真实体验风险。
latency、throughput、error rate 保证新方案在业务提升的同时没有拖垮系统健康。
