Return visit rate and long-term engagement trends reveal whether a change is just a short-lived novelty bump.
Negative feedback and user surveys catch real experience risks that pure metrics can miss.
Latency, throughput, and error rate confirm the new approach isn't tanking system health while it improves the business metric.
scenario: 新排序模型的 A/B 只盯 session 观看时长就上了，结果延迟涨、次周留存跌才被发现。
scenario_en: A ranking A/B was judged on session watch time alone, and only later did latency regressions and a week-two retention drop show up.

q: 推荐 A/B 实验中的 novelty effect（新奇效应）是什么？
options: 新系统因为内容新鲜而带来短期提升，但这个提升长期可能会回落
新模型在任何情况下都一定比旧模型差
novelty effect 只会出现在离线指标上
novelty effect 无法通过延长实验周期观察到
why: 用户可能暂时喜欢不一样的内容，过一段时间也会对新内容产生疲劳，实验要足够长并看长期指标。
why_en: A novelty effect is a temporary lift because the new recommender shows different content that may later become tiring.
options_en: The new system gets a short-term lift because the content feels fresh, but that lift can fade over time
The new model is guaranteed to be worse under every condition
A novelty effect can only show up in offline metrics
A novelty effect cannot be observed by running the experiment longer
q_en: What is a 'novelty effect' in a recommendation A/B test?

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组，对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into groups to compare the real-world effect of different versions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新系统因内容新鲜带来的短期提升，长期可能随用户适应而回落。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A novelty effect is a short-term lift from a new system feeling fresh, which can fade as users adapt.

optionExplanations: 新系统上线后内容显得新鲜，用户短期内多看一些很正常，但这个提升可能会随时间回落，不能只看头几天的数据下结论。
新模型不一定比旧模型差，novelty effect 说的是短期提升可能不持久，而不是新模型注定更差。
novelty effect 是真实用户行为的短期波动，线上指标同样会体现，不只是离线才有的现象。
延长实验周期、观察长期指标正是识别 novelty effect 消退最直接的方法，不是观察不到。
optionExplanations_en: A new system feels fresh right after launch, so a short-term bump in behavior is expected — but it can fade over time, so early-days numbers alone aren't conclusive.
The new model isn't necessarily worse — novelty effect just means an early lift may not hold, not that new models are always inferior.
Novelty effect is a real short-term shift in user behavior, so online metrics show it too — it isn't purely an offline artifact.
Running the experiment longer and watching the trend is exactly how you catch novelty effect fading, not something invisible to longer observation.
scenario: 新推荐模型上线第一周指标涨 5%，第三周就回落到基线附近。
scenario_en: A new recommender lifts metrics five percent in week one, then falls back near baseline by week three.

q: 推荐系统常见的反馈循环（feedback loop）问题包括什么？
options: 流行内容自我强化和内容茧房效应
标注员的标注速度会持续变慢
数据库索引会随时间自动失效
图片压缩效果会随时间变差
why: 推荐结果影响曝光，曝光又影响未来的训练数据和创作者行为，形成自我强化的循环。
why_en: Recommendation feedback loops include popularity bias, filter bubbles, and creators optimizing content for the algorithm.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Recommend[Model exposure] --> Clicks[User clicks]
  Clicks --> Logs[Training logs]
  Logs --> Train[Next model]
  Train --> Recommend
  Recommend --> Creator[Creator adapts]
  Creator --> Logs

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门内容因为已经热门而获得更多曝光，形成马太效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity bias is the rich-get-richer effect where already-popular items receive disproportionately more exposure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户长期只被展示越来越窄的一类内容的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A filter bubble is when a user is shown an increasingly narrow slice of content over time.

options_en: Popular content reinforcing itself and users getting stuck in a content filter bubble
Labelers gradually getting slower at labeling
Database indexes automatically expiring over time
Image compression quality degrading over time
q_en: What kinds of feedback-loop problems commonly show up in recommendation systems?
optionExplanations: 推荐结果影响曝光，曝光又反过来影响未来训练数据和创作者的行为选择，形成自我强化的流行内容循环。
标注员标注速度变慢是团队产能问题，跟推荐系统的反馈循环机制无关。
数据库索引自动失效是存储运维问题，不是推荐算法层面的反馈循环。
图片压缩效果变差是编解码问题，跟推荐系统的自我强化循环没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Recommendations shape exposure, and exposure in turn shapes future training data and creator behavior, forming a self-reinforcing loop around popular content.
Labelers slowing down is a team-capacity issue, unrelated to a recommender's feedback-loop mechanics.
Database indexes going stale is a storage/ops concern, not a feedback loop at the recommendation-algorithm level.
Image compression degrading is a codec issue, unrelated to a recommender's self-reinforcing loop.
scenario: 热门视频曝光越多，训练数据里的正样本越多，小创作者越来越召不回来。
scenario_en: The more a popular video is shown, the more positives it contributes to training, and small creators get recalled less and less.

scenario: 热门视频因为旧模型持续推荐而获得更多点击，新模型如果直接用这些日志训练，会继续学习“它热门”这件事本身。
q: 缓解这种 popularity feedback loop 的合理方法是什么？
options: counterfactual logging 加多样性约束去偏
单纯调高训练时用的学习率，寄望模型自己慢慢学会去偏差
把当前所有热门视频从候选池里整体下架
继续只用 CTR 一个指标来排序候选
whenOtherWins: 如果内容池本身可选项很少，diversity 约束能发挥的空间会比较有限。
why: 这些方法试图区分“用户真的喜欢”和“旧系统单纯给了更多曝光”两种情况，diversity 约束还能防止生态单一化。
why_en: Popularity feedback loops can be mitigated with counterfactual logging, propensity weighting, exploration traffic, and diversity constraints.
tradeoff: 去偏训练/多样性约束的生态健康收益 vs 短期参与度指标的下降风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录用户对未展示内容可能反馈的技术，用于估计和纠偏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual logging estimates how a user would have responded to items that were never shown.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按曝光概率的倒数给样本加权，纠正曝光偏差的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inverse-propensity weighting reweights logged examples by the inverse of their exposure probability to correct exposure bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，展示中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, click-through rate, is the fraction of impressions that get clicked.

options_en: Counterfactual logging combined with diversity constraints
Simply raise the learning rate used in training and hope the model somehow learns to debias on its own
Pull every currently popular video out of the candidate pool entirely
Keep ranking candidates by CTR as the only metric
q_en: What is a reasonable way to mitigate this popularity feedback loop?
scenario_en: Popular videos get more clicks because the old model kept recommending them; if the new model trains directly on these logs, it keeps re-learning "this is popular" as a signal in itself.
optionExplanations: counterfactual logging 记录曝光时的真实排序上下文，配合多样性约束，能区分用户是真喜欢还是单纯被旧系统多曝光，同时防止内容单一化。
单纯调高学习率不会让模型自己学会区分曝光偏差和真实偏好，反而可能让训练更不稳定。
把热门视频整体下架是过度反应，会连带损失真正受欢迎、值得继续曝光的内容。
继续只用 CTR 排序完全没有纠偏，热门视频会因为曝光多、点击多而持续被强化。
optionExplanations_en: Counterfactual logging captures the real exposure context at serving time, and paired with a diversity constraint, it can separate genuine preference from mere over-exposure by the old system while keeping content from converging on one type.
Simply raising the learning rate doesn't teach the model to separate exposure bias from real preference, and can make training less stable instead.
Pulling every popular video from the pool outright is an overcorrection that also removes genuinely well-liked content that deserves exposure.
Sticking with CTR alone does nothing to debias — popular videos keep getting reinforced simply because they were shown and clicked more.

scenario: 一个新用户刚注册，还没有任何观看历史，但产品要求第一屏就展示推荐。
q: 对新用户合理的冷启动策略是什么？
options: 先用 onboarding 兴趣分组、再逐步个性化
永久给这个用户展示完全随机的内容
等待 30 天，攒够行为数据后才展示任何推荐
固定只给新用户推荐时长最长的视频
whenOtherWins: 如果产品允许非个性化入口，展示全球或地区热门榜也可以作为更简单的起点。
why: 冷启动先用能拿到的信息和相似人群的行为打底，随着互动信号到来再逐步转向个性化。
why_en: Cold-start users can be bootstrapped with onboarding preferences and coarse similar-user clusters until enough behavior data accumulates.
tradeoff: 冷启动阶段推荐的相关性 vs 缺乏个性化数据带来的不确定性

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新内容缺少历史行为数据、难以个性化的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is the period when a new user or new item lacks the behavioral data needed for personalization.

options_en: Bucket by onboarding interests, then personalize over time
Show this user completely random content forever
Wait 30 days until enough behavior data accumulates before showing any recommendation
Always recommend new users the longest available videos
q_en: What is a reasonable cold-start strategy for a new user?
scenario_en: A user just signed up with no watch history at all, but the product requires showing recommendations on the very first screen.
optionExplanations: 先靠 onboarding 时的粗粒度兴趣把新用户分进相似人群打底，再随着真实互动信号增多逐步转向个性化。
永久随机内容放弃了所有能拿到的信息，哪怕是粗粒度的 onboarding 兴趣，也比完全随机更有参考价值。
等 30 天才展示推荐会让新用户第一屏体验空白，不符合产品要求首屏就有推荐的约束。
固定推最长视频只是单一维度的猜测，不代表这个新用户真正的兴趣方向。
optionExplanations_en: Bucketing the new user into a similar-interest group from onboarding gives a starting point, then shifting toward personalization as real interaction signals accumulate.
Showing permanently random content throws away every available signal — even coarse onboarding interests beat pure randomness.
Waiting 30 days leaves the new user's first screen empty, which conflicts with the product requirement to show recommendations immediately.
Always recommending the longest videos is just a single-dimension guess that says nothing about this new user's real interests.

scenario: 一条新视频刚上传，还没有任何观看历史，但平台希望给新创作者公平的曝光机会。
q: 对新视频合理的冷启动策略是什么？
options: 用多模态内容特征估计受众，做受控探索曝光
永远不把新视频放进候选池
什么都不做，只等它自然变热门
一次性随机推给所有用户，不做曝光控制
whenOtherWins: 如果内容涉及较高的政策或安全风险，需要先经过审核或安全过滤，再进入受控探索。
why: 内容特征给出初始受众估计，受控探索收集行为信号，同时限制对现有用户体验的风险。
why_en: Cold-start videos should use content features and controlled exploration to gather initial engagement signals safely.
tradeoff: 给新内容公平曝光机会 vs 控制探索流量对用户体验的风险
options_en: Estimate the audience from multimodal content features, then expose it through controlled exploration
Never add the new video to the candidate pool at all
Do nothing and just wait for it to go viral naturally
Push it to every user at once with no exposure control
q_en: What is a reasonable cold-start strategy for a new video?
scenario_en: A video was just uploaded with no watch history at all, and the platform wants to give new creators a fair chance at exposure.
optionExplanations: 用标题、缩略图、音频这类多模态内容特征先估计可能受众，再做受控探索曝光，收集真实互动信号验证。
永远不放进候选池等于新视频永远没有曝光机会，跟给新创作者公平机会的目标正好相反。
什么都不做等它自然变热门，在没有初始曝光的情况下几乎不可能发生，新视频会被埋没。
一次性随机推给所有用户没有曝光控制，一旦内容质量不佳会伤害大量用户的体验。
optionExplanations_en: Use multimodal content features like title, thumbnail, and audio to estimate the likely audience first, then serve controlled, exploratory exposure to gather real engagement signal.
Never adding it to the candidate pool means the new video never gets any exposure at all, the opposite of giving new creators a fair shot.
Doing nothing and waiting for it to go viral almost never happens without some initial exposure — the video just gets buried.
Blasting it to every user at once with no exposure control risks hurting a lot of users' experience if the content turns out weak.

q: 推荐系统里的 explore/exploit tradeoff 具体指什么？
options: 在已知喜欢的内容和可能发现新兴趣之间平衡
在 CPU 和 GPU 资源之间做平衡
在训练集和测试集之间混合标签
在删除内容和封禁账号之间做选择
why: 只做 exploit 会让推荐变窄和无聊，只做 explore 会显得随机、打扰用户，需要按位置和用户阶段分配探索预算。
why_en: Explore-exploit balances safe known-good recommendations against exploratory items that might reveal new interests.
tradeoff: 利用已知偏好的确定收益 vs 探索新兴趣的长期发现价值

termDefinitions.meaning: 在利用已知的好选项和尝试未知的新选项之间做平衡的经典问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Explore/exploit is the classic tradeoff between using known-good options and trying unknown ones that might be better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 适合并行矩阵运算的加速硬件，是工程资源分配问题，不是 explore/exploit 概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU, Graphics Processing Unit, is accelerator hardware for parallel math — an engineering resource question, not the explore/exploit concept.

options_en: Balancing content the user is known to like against content that might reveal a new interest
Balancing CPU and GPU resources
Mixing labels between the training set and the test set
Choosing between deleting content and banning an account
q_en: What does the explore/exploit tradeoff mean in a recommendation system?
optionExplanations: explore/exploit 说的是在已经确定用户喜欢的内容和可能发现的新兴趣之间做平衡，纯利用会让推荐变窄，纯探索会显得随机打扰。
CPU 和 GPU 资源分配是算力调度问题，跟用户兴趣的探索与利用完全是两回事。
训练集和测试集混合标签是数据泄漏问题，属于评估方法论范畴，不是 explore/exploit。
删除内容和封禁账号是内容安全和治理决策，跟推荐策略里的探索利用权衡无关。
optionExplanations_en: Explore/exploit is about balancing content the user is already known to like against the chance to surface a new interest — pure exploitation narrows recommendations, pure exploration feels random and intrusive.
Allocating CPU versus GPU is a compute-scheduling problem, unrelated to balancing exploration and exploitation of user interests.
Mixing labels between train and test sets is a data-leakage issue that belongs to evaluation methodology, not explore/exploit.
Removing content or banning accounts is a trust-and-safety decision, unrelated to the explore/exploit tradeoff in ranking strategy.
scenario: 只推用户已知兴趣时点击率最高，但一个月后用户的兴趣面明显变窄了。
scenario_en: Serving only known interests maximizes click rate, but a month later the users’ interest range has visibly narrowed.

scenario: 推荐列表第 1 位对用户体验影响很大，需要保持稳定；第 5 位风险较低，可以用来试探用户的新兴趣。
q: 应该如何为不同推荐位置分配探索预算？
options: 按位置分配探索预算（contextual bandit）
对所有推荐位置都用完全相同的随机探索比例分配
全部位置都不做任何探索，只做利用不冒险
只针对新上传视频做探索，其余位置全部固定
whenOtherWins: 如果产品场景要求完全确定性或有强合规约束，整体探索比例应该更保守。
why: 高位对体验影响大应该更保守，低位可以更多探索；bandit 类方法能在短期损失和长期学习之间取舍。
why_en: Different recommendation slots can carry different exploration budgets, often implemented with contextual bandits or Thompson sampling.
tradeoff: 顶部位置的体验稳定性 vs 底部位置的探索学习收益
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Exploit[Known good] --> Mix[Slot policy]
  Explore[New interests] --> Mix
  Mix --> User[User slate]
  User --> Feedback[Feedback]
  Feedback --> Learn[Better policy]

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据上下文特征动态调整探索和利用决策的强盗算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contextual bandit adjusts explore/exploit decisions using contextual features.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种贝叶斯强盗算法，按后验概率采样来决定探索哪个选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson sampling is a Bayesian bandit algorithm that samples from a posterior belief to decide what to explore.

options_en: A contextual bandit that gives each slot its own budget
Apply the exact same random exploration ratio to every single slot
Do no exploration anywhere and only exploit known-good picks
Only explore on brand-new uploads and keep every other slot fixed
q_en: How should exploration budget be allocated across different recommendation slots?
scenario_en: Slot 1 in the recommendation list has a big impact on user experience and needs to stay stable; slot 5 is lower-risk and can be used to probe for new interests.
optionExplanations: 用 contextual bandit 按每个推荐位单独分配探索预算，顶部保守求稳、底部多留空间试探新兴趣。
所有位置用相同随机探索比例，会让高位这种影响体验最大的位置也承担同样的探索风险。
全部位置都不探索只利用已知偏好，系统永远发现不了用户潜在的新兴趣。
只对新上传视频探索、其余位置固定，没有按位置本身的体验风险来分配探索预算。
optionExplanations_en: A contextual bandit assigns each slot its own exploration budget — conservative at the top to protect experience, more room to explore lower down.
Applying the same random exploration ratio everywhere puts the same exploration risk on high-impact top slots as on low-risk bottom ones.
Never exploring anywhere and only exploiting known preferences means the system can never discover a user's latent new interests.
Only exploring on brand-new uploads while keeping every other slot fixed ignores that exploration budget should track each slot's own experience risk.

q: Upper Confidence Bound（UCB）这类强盗算法在做选择时大致利用了什么原理？
options: 均值奖励加不确定性上界，偏好高潜力选项
只选择历史上曾经最热门的选项
只做完全随机的选择，不看历史
只根据视频长度做选择
why: UCB 用置信区间把探索价值显式加入选择分数；规模化实现时要处理海量 item 置信估计的成本。
why_en: UCB methods add an uncertainty bonus to the estimated reward, biasing selection toward promising but less-certain items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强盗算法的一种，用置信区间上界给不确定的选项额外的探索加分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UCB is a bandit algorithm that adds an uncertainty bonus to the estimated reward of less-certain options.

options_en: Adding an uncertainty bonus on top of the mean estimated reward, favoring high-potential options
Always picking whatever has historically been most popular
Choosing completely at random, ignoring history
Choosing based only on video length
q_en: Roughly what principle do bandit algorithms like Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) use when making a selection?
optionExplanations: UCB 把历史均值奖励加上一个不确定性上界，让还没被充分验证但潜力大的选项也有机会被选中。
只选历史最热门选项就是纯利用，完全放弃了探索，UCB 的意义正是要平衡这两者。
完全随机选择不看任何历史信息，浪费了已经积累的奖励数据，跟 UCB 的置信区间逻辑相反。
只按视频长度选择跟历史奖励和不确定性都无关，不是强盗算法真正依据的信号。
optionExplanations_en: UCB adds an uncertainty bound on top of the historical average reward, giving high-potential but under-tested options a real shot at being picked.
Always picking the historically most popular option is pure exploitation with no exploration at all — the whole point of UCB is balancing the two.
Choosing completely at random ignores accumulated reward data entirely, the opposite of UCB's confidence-bound logic.
Choosing purely by video length ignores both historical reward and uncertainty — it isn't a signal a bandit algorithm actually uses.
scenario: 新上传视频只有几十次曝光，你要在这些不确定候选和已知高分候选之间分配曝光位。
scenario_en: A freshly uploaded video has only tens of impressions, and you must split slots between uncertain candidates and known winners.

q: 为什么探索策略应该按用户或兴趣领域分别调整，而不是对所有用户用同一个探索比例？
options: 同一用户在不同兴趣领域的不确定性不同，个性化探索更高效
所有用户理论上都应该被同样随机地对待
探索策略只对新用户有意义，对老用户完全没用
按分段调整探索会导致所有反馈信号丢失
why: 探索预算 = 每屏曝光位数 × 探索比例；新用户不确定性高、探索回报大，重度用户同样比例只是打扰。代价是探索位让出即时收益。
why_en: Exploration budget is slots per screen times an exploration rate, so you spend it where uncertainty is high — new users and cold interest areas — because on a heavy user the same rate mostly just costs you a slot.
options_en: The same user has different amounts of uncertainty across interest areas, so personalized exploration is more efficient
In theory every user should be treated with the same randomness
Exploration strategy only matters for new users, not returning ones
Adjusting exploration by segment would cause all feedback signal to be lost
q_en: Why should exploration be tuned separately by user or interest area, instead of using the same exploration ratio for every user?
optionExplanations: 同一用户在不同兴趣领域积累的互动数据量不一样，不确定性也不同，按领域个性化分配探索预算能减少不必要打扰、提高发现价值。
所有用户理论上同样随机对待，忽略了老用户已经积累的信号比新用户丰富得多这个事实。
老用户在新的兴趣领域同样存在不确定性，探索策略不是只对新用户才有意义。
按分段调整探索预算只是改变探索的分配方式，不会导致任何反馈信号丢失。
optionExplanations_en: The same user has different amounts of accumulated signal, and therefore different uncertainty, across interest areas — personalizing the exploration budget per area cuts wasted disruption and raises discovery value.
Treating every user identically at random ignores that returning users already have far richer accumulated signal than new ones.
Returning users still carry uncertainty in interest areas that are new to them — exploration isn't only useful for brand-new users.
Adjusting exploration budget by segment just changes how exploration is allocated — it doesn't cause any feedback signal to be lost.
scenario: 重度用户历史行为上万条、新用户只有 3 条，你要给两类用户定探索比例。
scenario_en: Heavy users have tens of thousands of history events while new users have three, and you must set an exploration rate for each.

q: 按正确顺序排列大规模视频推荐的在线请求处理流程。
steps: 重 ranker 用完整特征精排
多个 candidate generator 并行召回
轻 ranker 高召回缩小候选
why: 先广泛召回，再用便宜模型保留潜在好候选，重模型精排，最后在 slate 层处理多样性和业务约束。
why_en: The online recommender retrieves candidates, filters them with a light ranker, scores them with a heavy ranker, and reranks the slate.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Gen[Candidate generators] --> Light[Light ranker]
  Light --> Heavy[Heavy ranker]
  Heavy --> Slate[Reranker slate]
  Slate --> Logs[Feedback logs]
  Logs --> Train[Next training]
q_en: Put the online request-processing pipeline for a large-scale video recommender in the correct order.

q: 按合理顺序排列视频推荐系统的训练流程。
steps: 收集显式/隐式/上下文数据
训练两塔或其他召回模型
训练轻 ranker 和重多任务 ranker
用线上 A/B 和长期指标校验 value model
why: 数据定义监督信号，召回先保证候选覆盖，ranker 优化排序，最终由线上指标验证业务权重是否合理。
why_en: Video recommendation training starts with feedback data, then retrieval models, ranking models, and finally online validation of the value model.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Data[Feedback and context] --> Retrieve[Train retrieval]
  Retrieve --> Rank[Train rankers]
  Rank --> Value[Calibrate value model]
  Value --> AB[Online AB]
  AB --> Data
q_en: Put the training pipeline for a video recommendation system in a reasonable order.

scenario: 你要向面试官说明向量召回 candidate generator 的在线核心逻辑。
q: 下面这段伪代码表达的是什么？
options: 重 ranker 对候选做最终精确打分
用用户向量在视频 ANN 索引中检索候选
对预测分数做 Platt calibration
对稀有事件做 Bayesian smoothing
whenOtherWins: 如果需要对少量候选做精确重排，cross-encoder 或重 ranker 会更合适，而不是继续用 ANN 检索。
why: 在线只需要用用户塔算出向量，再去离线建好的视频 ANN 索引里做近邻检索，适合大规模候选生成。
why_en: The code retrieves video candidates by searching an ANN index with the online user embedding.
tradeoff: ANN 检索的低延迟规模化 vs 检索结果的近似性（不保证严格最优）

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，在海量向量里快速找出最相似的几个，不保证绝对精确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN, approximate nearest neighbor search, quickly retrieves the closest vectors from a huge index without scanning everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在样本量很小时用先验信息平滑估计值的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bayesian smoothing uses prior information to stabilize estimates when the sample size is small.

options_en: The heavy ranker giving candidates a final precise score
Searching a video ANN index with the user embedding to retrieve candidates
Applying Platt calibration to prediction scores
Applying Bayesian smoothing to rare events
q_en: What does this pseudocode express?
scenario_en: You need to explain to the interviewer the core online logic of a vector-retrieval candidate generator.
optionExplanations: 重 ranker 精确打分是在候选已经被检索出来之后才做的事，跟这段在线检索本身的逻辑不是同一步。
服务时只需要跑一次用户塔拿到向量，再拿这个向量去查已经建好的近邻索引，检索本身不涉及打分。
Platt calibration 是训练完之后校准分数用的，不是向量检索这一步在做的事。
Bayesian smoothing 是给稀有事件的统计估计做平滑，跟 ANN 近邻检索完全是两个机制。
optionExplanations_en: The heavy ranker's precise scoring happens after candidates are already retrieved — that's a different step from this online-retrieval logic itself.
At serving time it only needs one pass through the user tower to get a vector, then looks that vector up in a prebuilt nearest-neighbor index — retrieval itself involves no scoring.
Platt calibration adjusts scores after training is done, not something the vector-retrieval step is doing.
Bayesian smoothing is for smoothing statistical estimates of rare events, a completely different mechanism from ANN nearest-neighbor search.

q: staff-level 候选人在视频推荐系统设计中应主动覆盖哪些系统性风险？（多选）
options: 反馈循环和 popularity bias
cold start（新用户/新内容）
position bias 和数据质量问题
创作者生态健康和推荐多样性
why: 高级别的答案不只谈模型结构，还要主动谈数据、评估方法和生态副作用。
why_en: Staff-level recommender answers should proactively cover feedback loops, cold start, position bias and data quality, and ecosystem health.
options_en: Feedback loops and popularity bias
Cold start for new users and new content
Position bias and data-quality issues
Creator ecosystem health and recommendation diversity
q_en: Which systemic risks should a staff-level candidate proactively cover when designing a video recommendation system? (select all)

termDefinitions.meaning: 展示位置越靠前的内容越容易被点击，导致训练日志系统性偏向旧系统的排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is the tendency for higher-ranked items to get more clicks, which skews training logs toward the old ranking system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门内容因为已经热门而获得更多曝光，形成马太效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity bias is the rich-get-richer effect where already-popular items receive disproportionately more exposure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新内容缺少历史行为数据、难以个性化的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is the period when a new user or new item lacks the behavioral data needed for personalization.

optionExplanations: 覆盖反馈循环和 popularity bias，能防止系统把「曝光多」误当成「用户真喜欢」，避免内容持续同质化。
覆盖 cold start，能确保新用户和新内容不会因为缺乏历史数据而被系统长期忽视。
覆盖 position bias 和数据质量问题，能防止训练数据本身的偏差被模型当成真实偏好学进去。
覆盖创作者生态健康和推荐多样性，能防止推荐系统只优化短期参与度而拖垮长期供给。
optionExplanations_en: Covering feedback loops and popularity bias stops the system from mistaking heavy exposure for genuine preference and drifting toward homogeneous content.
Covering cold start ensures new users and new content aren't permanently ignored just because they lack history yet.
Covering position bias and data quality stops the model from learning the training data's own bias as if it were real preference.
Covering creator ecosystem health and diversity stops the system from optimizing short-term engagement at the expense of long-term content supply.
scenario: 视频推荐上线一年，模型指标持续上涨，创作者却在流失、推荐面也越来越窄。
scenario_en: A year after launch model metrics keep climbing, yet creators are churning and recommendations keep getting narrower.

q: 为什么说现代视频推荐系统的瓶颈往往不只是模型架构本身？
options: 数据质量、评估方法、反馈循环和整体系统设计同样决定推荐系统的成败
模型架构的选择完全不重要，随便挑哪种架构都完全可以
只要模型参数量足够庞大，其他环节都完全不用管
线上的 A/B 实验对推荐系统来说没有任何实际意义
why: 再强的模型也只能学习日志给它的偏差和候选池；推荐系统的成功需要数据、召回、实验和生态共同健康。
why_en: Modern recommendation success depends on data quality, evaluation, feedback loops, and overall system design, not just model architecture.
options_en: Data quality, evaluation methodology, feedback loops, and overall system design equally determine success
The choice of model architecture is completely unimportant; any architecture picked at random works just as well
As long as the model has a huge enough parameter count, nothing else needs any attention at all
Online A/B experiments have no real value at all for recommendation systems
q_en: Why is the bottleneck in modern video recommendation systems often not just the model architecture itself?

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组，对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into groups to compare the real-world effect of different versions.

optionExplanations: 数据质量、评估方法、反馈循环和整体系统设计跟模型架构同样重要，任何一环拖后腿都会限制整体效果。
模型架构完全不重要这个说法过于极端，架构选择依然会影响能不能学到复杂交互。
参数量再大，训练数据有偏、评估方法不完整，模型学到的仍然是错误或片面的目标。
线上 A/B 实验恰恰是验证离线改进是否真正转化为用户价值的关键环节，不是没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Data quality, evaluation methodology, feedback loops, and overall system design matter just as much as model architecture — any weak link caps the whole system's results.
Saying architecture doesn't matter at all is too extreme — architecture choice still affects whether complex interactions can be learned.
No matter how many parameters a model has, biased training data or incomplete evaluation still means it's learning the wrong or partial objective.
Online A/B testing is exactly the step that verifies whether offline improvements actually translate into real user value — it's far from meaningless.
scenario: 团队把 ranker 换成更大的 Transformer，离线 AUC 涨了，线上指标却几乎没动。
scenario_en: The team swaps in a much larger Transformer ranker, offline AUC improves, and online metrics barely move.

scenario: 默认前提是轻排层没有 GPU、只能用 CPU 树模型；现在假设这一层拿到了 GPU 预算。
scenario_en: The default assumption is the light-ranker layer has no GPU and runs a CPU tree model; now assume this layer gets a GPU budget.
q: 有 GPU 的前提下，为什么值得把轻 ranker 换成从重 ranker 蒸馏的 skinny MLP？
q_en: Given a GPU, why is it worth swapping the light ranker for a skinny MLP distilled from the heavy ranker?
options: 它能复用重 ranker 从类别特征学到的宽 embedding，用小算力逼近精排的判断
蒸馏后的 MLP 参数量一定比 GBDT 更少，因此保证在任何硬件上都跑得更快更省钱
MLP 能直接读原始视频文件，于是可以省掉整个候选生成和 embedding 阶段
蒸馏能让轻排完全等价于重排，于是精排这一层可以直接删掉
options_en: It reuses the wide embeddings the heavy ranker learned from categorical features to approximate heavy-ranker judgments cheaply
A distilled MLP always has fewer parameters than a GBDT, so it is guaranteed to run faster and cheaper on any hardware
An MLP can read raw video files directly, so it removes the whole candidate-generation and embedding stage
Distillation makes the light ranker fully equivalent to the heavy ranker, so the heavy-ranking stage can be deleted
tradeoff: 轻排模型：树模型(GBDT) vs 蒸馏 MLP —— 部署算力 vs 表示复用能力
whenOtherWins: 当轻排层只有 CPU、算力紧张时，GBDT/LightGBM 在结构化特征上以亚毫秒延迟取胜，反而是更划算的选择。
why: GPU 紧张才默认树模型；有 GPU 时蒸馏 MLP 能继承重 ranker 学到的宽 embedding，用小算力逼近精排质量，代价是多维护一条蒸馏管线。
why_en: With a GPU, a skinny MLP distilled from the heavy ranker reuses its learned wide embeddings to get near heavy-ranker quality cheaply, at the cost of maintaining a distillation pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(教师)的输出训练一个小模型(学生)，让小模型逼近大模型质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distillation trains a small student model on a large teacher model's outputs so the student approaches the teacher's quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层感知机：由若干全连接层堆叠的前馈神经网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) is a feed-forward neural network of stacked fully-connected layers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升决策树：逐棵拟合残差的树集成模型，擅长结构化特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GBDT (Gradient Boosted Decision Tree) is a tree ensemble that fits residuals stage by stage, strong on structured features.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从高基数类别特征(如 creator_id)学到的稠密向量表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wide embedding is the dense vector representation learned for high-cardinality categorical features such as creator_id.

optionExplanations: 有 GPU 时，轻排能复用精排的宽向量表示，用小模型把打分拉近精排水平。
参数少不必然更快：GBDT 在 CPU 上本就亚毫秒，蒸馏 MLP 的优势前提是有 GPU，不是「更省」。
排序模型吃的是预计算好的 embedding，读原始视频文件既慢又不可行，也不省候选生成。
轻排是为高吞吐做的近似过滤，永远无法等价精排，删掉精排会丢掉高阶交互。
optionExplanations_en: With a GPU the light stage can reuse the heavy model's wide vector representations, pulling its scores close to heavy-ranker level with a tiny model.
Fewer params doesn't mean faster: GBDT is already sub-ms on CPU; the MLP's edge assumes a GPU, not lower cost.
Rankers consume precomputed embeddings; reading raw video files is slow and infeasible and doesn't remove candidate generation.
The light ranker is an approximate high-throughput filter and can never equal the heavy one; deleting it loses high-order interactions.

scenario: 候选人提议直接用矩阵分解/协同过滤作为线上主排序模型，而不是当 baseline。
scenario_en: A candidate proposes using matrix factorization / collaborative filtering as the production main ranker rather than a baseline.
q: 为什么把矩阵分解/协同过滤当生产主模型(而非 baseline)在现代视频推荐里会吃亏？
q_en: Why does using matrix factorization / collaborative filtering as the production main model (not a baseline) underperform in modern video recommendation?
options: 它只学用户-物品交互矩阵，用不上当前视频、会话序列和内容特征，已非 SOTA
它会为每个用户和视频各训练一个专属深度网络，因此训练成本高到线上跑不起来
它需要 GPU 和 transformer 才能训练，推理延迟远超 250ms 预算
它无法产生任何候选，只能在重排阶段对已排好的 slate 做微调
options_en: It only learns the user-item interaction matrix, ignoring the current video, session sequence and content features — no longer SOTA
It trains a separate dedicated deep network per user and per video, so training cost is too high to run online
It needs a GPU and a transformer to train, and its inference latency far exceeds the 250ms budget
It cannot generate any candidates and can only fine-tune an already-ranked slate in the re-ranking stage
why: MF/CF 只吃用户-物品交互矩阵，接不进当前观看视频、会话序列和 engagement 这些两条腿输入，已非 SOTA；它仍适合当对照 baseline，但当主模型会系统性欠拟合上下文。
why_en: MF/CF only ingests the user-item interaction matrix and can't take the current video, session sequence and engagement inputs, so it's no longer SOTA — fine as a baseline, but as the main model it systematically underfits context.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户-物品评分矩阵分解成两组低维向量的乘积来预测偏好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Matrix factorization decomposes the user-item rating matrix into two sets of low-rank vectors to predict preference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 仅凭历史交互「跟你相似的人喜欢什么」来推荐，不依赖内容特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends via 'people similar to you liked X' using only interaction history, not content features.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前最优水平的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOTA (State Of The Art) means the current best-performing approach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 简单参照模型，用来衡量复杂方案是否真的值得。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is a simple reference model used to judge whether a complex approach is actually worth it.

optionExplanations: MF/CF 只看交互矩阵，喂不进当前视频/序列/内容特征，做主模型必然欠拟合上下文。
MF/CF 恰恰不训练深网络，它是廉价的线性分解，「贵到跑不起」说反了。
MF/CF 是轻量线性方法，不需要 transformer，延迟根本不是它落选主模型的原因。
MF/CF 完全可以做候选生成器，「只能微调 slate」不是它的局限。
optionExplanations_en: MF/CF sees only the interaction matrix and can't take the current video/sequence/content features, so as a main model it underfits context.
MF/CF trains no deep network — it is a cheap linear factorization, so 'too expensive to run' is backwards.
MF/CF is a lightweight linear method needing no transformer; latency is not why it's rejected as the main model.
MF/CF can perfectly well act as a candidate generator; 'only fine-tunes the slate' is not its limitation.

scenario: 新视频/新用户几乎没有行为标签，heavy ranker 的观看时长预测头几乎学不到东西。
scenario_en: New videos/users have almost no behavioral labels, so the heavy ranker's watch-time head has little to learn from.
q: 多任务的 heavy ranker 为什么能在冷启动(标签稀疏)时比单任务模型表现更好？
q_en: Why does a multitask heavy ranker handle cold start (sparse labels) better than a single-task model?
options: 任务间相关，某个头标签稀疏时可借相关任务的信号补足，缓解冷启动欠拟合
多任务会为每个新视频单独训练一个专属子模型，因此从此不再存在数据稀疏的问题
多任务把所有预测头合并成一个输出，从而减少了需要标注的样本总量
多任务能直接跳过重 ranker，用候选生成的 embedding 就完成排序
options_en: The tasks are correlated, so when one head's labels are sparse it borrows signal from related tasks, easing cold-start underfitting
Multitask trains a separate dedicated sub-model for every new video, so data sparsity simply stops existing
Multitask merges all prediction heads into one output, reducing the total number of samples that need labeling
Multitask lets you skip the heavy ranker and rank using the candidate-generation embeddings alone
why: 冷启动时单个头(如观看时长)标签稀疏；多任务让点击、完成率等相关头共享表示、互相提供辅助信号，从而补足稀疏头的学习，代价是各任务权重要调平衡。
why_en: In cold start a single head like watch-time has sparse labels; multitask lets correlated heads (click, completion) share representations and give auxiliary signal, filling in the sparse head — at the cost of tuning task weights.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个模型同时预测多个相关任务，共享底层表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multitask learning trains one model to predict several related tasks while sharing lower-layer representations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新内容缺少历史行为、难以个性化的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is the period when a new user or item lacks the behavioral history needed for personalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 来自其它相关任务、帮助主任务学到更好表示的梯度信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auxiliary signal is gradient from a related task that helps the main task learn better representations.

optionExplanations: 点击、完成率等头与观看时长相关，稀疏时互相借信号，正是多任务缓解冷启动的机制。
多任务是一个共享模型，不为每条新视频单训子模型；稀疏问题只是被缓解，不会消失。
多任务不是把输出合并省标注，各头仍各有标签，合并输出会丢掉任务特异信息。
多任务发生在重 ranker 内部，不能跳过重排；候选 embedding 精度不足以直接排序。
optionExplanations_en: Click and completion heads correlate with watch-time and lend signal when it's sparse — exactly how multitask eases cold start.
Multitask is one shared model, not a sub-model per video; sparsity is eased, not eliminated.
Multitask doesn't merge outputs to save labels; each head keeps its own labels, and merging would lose task-specific signal.
Multitask lives inside the heavy ranker and can't be skipped; candidate embeddings are too coarse to rank directly.

scenario: 团队要选一个离线指标，用来决定哪个模型值得推上线做 A/B 实验。
scenario_en: The team must pick an offline metric to decide which model is worth promoting to an online A/B test.
q: 为什么说离线指标本质是「近似移动靶」，选离线指标的唯一标准应该是什么？
q_en: Why are offline metrics essentially 'approximating a moving target', and what should the sole criterion for choosing one be?
options: 用户行为一直在变、离线只是近似，应选那些能预测线上实验成败的指标
离线指标其实绝对准确，只要离线 AUC 高线上就必然涨，因此可以直接跳过 A/B 实验
离线指标应该只看模型体积和推理延迟，与用户实际行为无关
离线指标越多越好，把所有能算的指标都堆上就能保证选对模型
options_en: User behavior keeps shifting and offline is only an approximation, so pick metrics that predict whether an online experiment will succeed
Offline metrics are actually exact, so a high offline AUC guarantees online gains and you can skip A/B testing entirely
Offline metrics should only track model size and inference latency, unrelated to real user behavior
More offline metrics are always better; pile on every computable metric and you're guaranteed to pick the right model
why: 用户行为是移动靶，任何离线指标都只是它的近似；因此选指标的唯一标准是它能不能预示线上 A/B 的成败，而非离线数值本身好看。
why_en: User behavior is a moving target, so any offline metric is just an approximation; the only criterion for choosing one is whether it predicts online A/B success, not how good the offline number looks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用历史日志、不上线就能算出的模型评估指标(如 NDCG、AUC)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offline metric is a model-evaluation score computed from historical logs without going live, such as NDCG or AUC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组、对比不同版本真实效果的线上实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users to compare the real effect of different versions online.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量排序/分类模型区分正负样本的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures how well a ranking/classification model separates positives from negatives.

optionExplanations: 行为是移动靶，离线永远近似；因此指标的价值在于它能否预示线上实验成败。
离线高不必然线上涨，novelty 效应和分布偏移都会让离线线上脱节，A/B 不能跳过。
只看体积和延迟是工程指标，回答不了「哪个模型更懂用户」，方向错了。
堆一堆离线指标不解决近似移动靶的本质，反而稀释判断，不保证选对。
optionExplanations_en: Behavior is a moving target and offline is always an approximation, so a metric's value is whether it predicts online success.
High offline doesn't guarantee online gains — novelty effects and distribution shift decouple them, so A/B can't be skipped.
Size and latency are engineering metrics; they can't answer 'which model understands users', so this is the wrong axis.
Piling on offline metrics doesn't fix the moving-target approximation and dilutes the decision, guaranteeing nothing.

scenario: 要在当前观看会话里，给每条候选视频算出一个排序分。
scenario_en: Within the current watching session, we must compute a ranking score for each candidate video.
q: 为什么 ranker 的输入要拆成「推荐上下文」和「候选视频」两条腿，而不是只喂一个用户向量？
q_en: Why is the ranker's input split into a 'recommendation context' leg and a 'candidate video' leg, rather than just one user vector?
options: 打分是上下文×候选的函数，两条腿才能对每条候选算出它与当前上下文的匹配分
只喂用户向量就够了，候选视频的信息在候选生成阶段已经用完，排序阶段不再需要
拆成两条腿是为了让模型参数量翻倍，从而机械地提高排序精度
两条腿的目的是把用户和视频存进同一张向量库，方便近邻检索
options_en: The score is a function of context × candidate, so two legs are what let it compute each candidate's match to the current context
One user vector is enough; candidate-video information was already used up in candidate generation and isn't needed at ranking
Splitting into two legs is meant to double the parameter count and mechanically raise ranking precision
The two legs exist to store users and videos in the same vector database for nearest-neighbor retrieval
why: 排序分是「上下文(当前视频+用户画像/历史)」与「每条候选视频」共同的函数；缺了候选这条腿，模型只能输出与候选无关的用户偏好，无法对逐条候选排序。
why_en: The score is a joint function of the context (current video + user profile/history) and each candidate video; drop the candidate leg and the model can only output candidate-agnostic user preference, unable to rank candidates one by one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前正在看的视频加用户画像与会话历史，作为排序的一条输入腿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The recommendation context is the currently-watched video plus the user's profile and session history, one input leg for ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选生成阶段送来的、等待排序打分的每条视频。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate is each video passed from candidate generation that awaits scoring by the ranker.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔与物品塔各产一个 embedding、用点积检索的召回结构，区别于逐条打分的排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-tower is a retrieval structure where a user tower and item tower each emit an embedding retrieved by dot product, distinct from per-candidate ranking.

optionExplanations: 排序分依赖上下文与候选的交互，两条腿才能对每条候选给出上下文相关的分数。
候选生成只做粗筛，排序恰恰要重新用候选视频的完整特征打分，信息远没用完。
翻倍参数不是拆腿的目的；两条腿是为建模交互，不是为堆参数。
用户+物品同库点积检索是 two-tower 召回的做法，排序阶段要逐条建模交互，不同层。
optionExplanations_en: The score depends on context-candidate interaction; two legs let it give each candidate a context-aware score.
Candidate generation only coarse-filters; ranking re-scores using each candidate's full features, so the info is far from used up.
Doubling parameters isn't the point; the two legs exist to model interaction, not to pile on parameters.
Storing user+item in one DB for dot-product retrieval is two-tower recall; ranking models per-candidate interaction, a different stage.

scenario: 一条视频已经积累了充足的观看、点赞和分享日志。
scenario_en: A video has already accumulated plenty of watch, like and share logs.
q: 对这条有充足行为日志的视频，排序更应该信任内容特征(标题/缩略图/主题)还是行为信号？
q_en: For this video with plenty of behavioral logs, should ranking trust content features (title/thumbnail/topic) or behavioral signals more?
options: 行为信号——内容只能冷读大致主题，难预测具体喜好，有行为时行为更准
内容特征——只要把标题和缩略图分析清楚，就能准确判断每个用户是否会喜欢这条视频
两者都不信任，直接按视频上传时间倒序排列对所有用户最公平
只信任创作者的订阅数，行为信号和内容特征都可以忽略
options_en: Behavioral signals — content only cold-reads a rough topic and can't predict specific taste, so with behavior available behavior is more accurate
Content features — once you analyze the title and thumbnail carefully you can accurately tell whether each user will like this video
Trust neither; sorting all users by upload time descending is the fairest option
Trust only the creator's subscriber count; both behavioral signals and content features can be ignored
tradeoff: 视频特征：内容特征 vs 行为信号 —— 冷读可得性 vs 偏好预测准确度
whenOtherWins: 新上传、还没有行为日志的视频(冷启动)只能靠多模态内容特征冷读来做初始曝光，此时内容特征反而是主力。
why: 内容特征只能冷读大致主题和制作质量，难预测具体喜好；一旦有行为日志，推荐系统更信行为信号。代价是完全无行为的新视频只能退回内容特征。
why_en: Content features only cold-read rough topic and production quality and can't predict specific taste; once behavioral logs exist the system trusts behavior more — at the cost that a brand-new video with no behavior must fall back on content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从视频本身抽取的标题、缩略图、音频、主题 embedding 等特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-based features are extracted from the video itself: title, thumbnail, audio, topic embeddings and so on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 仅凭内容本身、无行为数据地猜测用户是否喜欢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold reading means guessing whether users will like a video from its content alone, with no behavioral data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时利用缩略图、文本、音频等多种模态的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multimodal means a model that uses several modalities at once, such as thumbnail, text and audio.

optionExplanations: 有行为日志时行为信号最能反映真实喜好，内容只能给出粗略主题，故信行为。
内容冷读预测不了具体喜好；标题缩略图看着对味也常与真实观看行为背离，这是常见误解。
按上传时间排序放弃了所有个性化信号，既不准也谈不上公平，纯属逃避排序。
只看订阅数忽略了逐条视频的行为与内容证据，粒度太粗，会漏掉爆款和长尾。
optionExplanations_en: With behavioral logs, behavior best reflects real taste while content gives only a rough topic, so trust behavior.
Content cold-reading can't predict specific taste; an on-topic title/thumbnail often diverges from real watch behavior — a common misconception.
Sorting by upload time discards all personalization signal — neither accurate nor fair, just avoiding ranking.
Subscriber count alone ignores per-video behavioral and content evidence; too coarse, it misses both hits and the long tail.

scenario: 上线了 explore/exploit 策略，要向面试官证明探索本身有价值，而不是白白牺牲参与度。
scenario_en: An explore/exploit strategy is live; you must show the interviewer that exploration itself adds value rather than just sacrificing engagement.
q: 怎么衡量探索策略本身是否有效，而不只是看短期参与度有没有掉？
q_en: How do you measure whether the exploration strategy itself is effective, not just whether short-term engagement dropped?
options: 看发现新兴趣、新内容的长期收益能否抵回短期参与度的让利
只要短期 session 观看时长没有下降，就足以说明探索策略完全成功，不需要别的指标
统计探索位一共占用了多少屏幕像素和曝光次数，占得越多就说明探索越有效
只要模型的离线 AUC 指标有所提升就算成功，与线上长期表现完全无关
options_en: Whether the long-term gains of surfacing new interests and new content repay the short-term engagement given up
As long as short-term session watch time doesn't drop, exploration is fully successful and no other metric is needed
Count how many screen pixels and impressions the exploration slots occupy; the more they take, the more effective exploration is
As long as the model's offline AUC metric improves it counts as success, wholly unrelated to long-term online behavior
why: 探索会主动让出即时 engagement 去换长期发现；衡量它有效与否，要对比长期 discovery 收益(用户被带出信息茧、新内容被发现)是否值回短期让利，而非只盯短期指标。
why_en: Exploration deliberately trades away immediate engagement for long-term discovery; measuring it means checking whether long-term discovery gains (users pulled out of filter bubbles, new content surfaced) repay the short-term give-up, not just watching short-term metrics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在推荐已知会喜欢的内容(利用)与试探未知新兴趣(探索)之间取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Explore/exploit is the tradeoff between recommending known-liked content (exploit) and probing unknown new interests (explore).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户借探索发现新兴趣、新内容或新创作者的长期收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Discovery is the long-term gain of users finding new interests, content or creators through exploration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击、观看时长、留存等衡量用户参与度的短期行为信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement is short-term behavior like clicks, watch time and retention that measures user participation.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量模型区分正负样本能力的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of how well a model separates positives from negatives.

optionExplanations: 探索的价值兑现在未来，要看发现新兴趣的收益能不能补回当下少赚的参与度。
短期时长不掉只说明没伤害，证明不了探索带来了长期发现，指标片面。
屏幕像素是投入量不是效果，占得多不等于探索有效，方向错了。
离线 AUC 反映不了探索的长期发现价值，探索效果只能在线上长期观测。
optionExplanations_en: Exploration pays off later, so the test is whether surfacing new interests earns back the engagement given up now.
Flat short-term watch time only shows no harm; it can't prove exploration produced long-term discovery — a one-sided metric.
Screen pixels are input, not outcome; more pixels don't mean effective exploration — the wrong axis.
Offline AUC can't reflect exploration's long-term discovery value; that effect is only visible online over time.

scenario: 十亿量级视频，每次 Up Next 要在 250ms 延迟预算内从候选里检索并打分(250ms 是给定的产品目标)。
scenario_en: Billion-scale videos; each Up Next must retrieve from candidates and score within a 250ms latency budget (the 250ms is a given product target).
q: senior 级 serving 优化里，除了量化和 GPU，为什么还必须上高效近邻检索和 embedding 压缩？
q_en: Beyond quantization and GPUs, why must senior-level serving also add efficient nearest-neighbor search and embedding compression?
options: 对十亿全精度向量做精确最近邻会撑爆延迟和内存，需 ANN 索引+压缩向量才进 250ms
因为量化和 GPU 这两种手段其实都只在离线训练阶段才有用，到了在线推理阶段就完全派不上用场了
上了高效近邻检索之后，整个系统就可以彻底不再需要候选生成这一整个阶段了
embedding 压缩的真正目的其实是为了把离线 NDCG 排序指标算得更高一些
options_en: Exact nearest neighbor over a billion full-precision vectors blows the latency and memory budget; ANN indexing plus compressed vectors is what fits 250ms
Because quantization and GPUs are actually only useful during offline training and become entirely useless at online inference time
Once efficient nearest-neighbor search is in place, the whole system no longer needs the candidate-generation stage at all
The real purpose of embedding compression is actually to compute a somewhat higher offline NDCG ranking metric
why: 十亿量级下逐条精确算最近邻会撑爆 250ms 延迟预算和向量库内存；用 ANN(近似最近邻)索引把检索降到亚线性、再压缩 embedding 省内存，才凑得进预算。代价是近似召回略有损失。
why_en: At billion scale, exact per-vector nearest neighbor blows the 250ms budget and vector-store memory; an ANN index cuts retrieval to sub-linear and compressing embeddings saves memory to fit the budget — at the cost of slightly lossy recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：牺牲少量准确率换取亚线性检索速度的索引方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) is indexing that trades a little accuracy for sub-linear retrieval speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用低比特或降维把向量存得更小，减少内存和带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding compression stores vectors smaller via low-bit or dimensionality reduction to cut memory and bandwidth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型或向量的浮点数降到低比特整数以省内存、提吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers a model or vector's floats to low-bit integers to save memory and raise throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益：衡量排序结果好坏、越靠前相关项权重越高的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is an offline ranking metric that rewards putting relevant items higher.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器，擅长并行计算，常用于加速模型训练与推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is a highly parallel processor commonly used to accelerate model training and inference.

optionExplanations: 十亿全精度向量精确检索会爆延迟与内存，ANN+压缩把检索和存储降下来才进 250ms。
量化和 GPU 主要就是服务优化手段，正是用在推理侧的，说只对训练有用是反的。
近邻检索本身就是候选生成的一部分，不是它的替代品，砍不掉候选生成。
embedding 压缩是省内存换延迟的服务优化，与提高离线 NDCG 无关。
optionExplanations_en: Exact search over a billion full-precision vectors blows latency and memory; ANN plus compression brings both down to fit 250ms.
Quantization and GPUs are serving optimizations used at inference — saying they only help training is backwards.
Nearest-neighbor search is part of candidate generation, not a replacement, so it can't remove that stage.
Embedding compression trades memory for latency at serving time and has nothing to do with raising offline NDCG.
